title: Eyes Wide Shut
synopsis: Kubrick's final film, finished six days before his death, sends Tom Cruise's Manhattan doctor on a nocturnal odyssey through the city after his wife (Nicole Kidman) confesses an unconsummated fantasy — culminating at a masked orgy of an exclusive secret society and a marriage that may or may not survive what each spouse has now seen.

title: Mildred Pierce
synopsis: Joan Crawford's career-defining performance as the self-made Mildred Pierce — who sacrifices everything for a daughter who weaponizes every gift against her — transforms a murder-mystery framework into a corrosive portrait of maternal love as its own destruction.

title: Brief Encounter
synopsis: David Lean's masterpiece of restraint follows two married strangers whose deepening, never-consummated love affair at a railway station cafe is conducted entirely in glances and silences, the film understanding that the most devastating romances end not with catastrophe but with the quiet return to ordinary life.

title: It's a Wonderful Life
synopsis: Frank Capra's luminous fable sends a despairing George Bailey, rescued from Christmas Eve suicide by a bumbling angel, on a tour of Bedford Falls without him, James Stewart's performance moving from anguished desperation to luminous gratitude in what became the most beloved holiday film in American history.

title: The Best Years of Our Lives
synopsis: William Wyler's monumental homecoming drama follows three WWII veterans struggling to reintegrate into a civilian world that has changed as irrevocably as they have, earning seven Academy Awards and standing as the definitive American film about the cost of war beyond the battlefield.

title: Notorious
synopsis: Hitchcock's most perfectly balanced romantic thriller sends Ingrid Bergman's woman-with-a-notorious-past undercover among Nazi agents in Rio de Janeiro, where her government handler Cary Grant and she fall irreversibly in love, the tension arising from the impossibility of separating espionage from eros.

title: Gentleman's Agreement
synopsis: Elia Kazan's bracingly contemporary drama sends Gregory Peck's journalist undercover as Jewish to expose antisemitism in polite American society, discovering that the prejudice he documents is not confined to overt bigots but embedded in the social codes of those who would consider themselves enlightened.

title: Treasure of the Sierra Madre
synopsis: John Huston's rugged masterpiece follows two drifting Americans and a wizened old prospector into the Sierra Madre mountains in search of gold, the treasure becoming the agent of their undoing through greed's ancient alchemical corrosion — Humphrey Bogart's descent from desperation to paranoid delusion among his greatest achievements.

title: Red River
synopsis: Howard Hawks's sprawling Western follows cattle baron Tom Dunson and his headstrong adopted son Matthew on a brutal Texas-to-Missouri drive, the men's mutual devotion curdling into violent opposition as Dunson's tyrannical leadership grows intolerable — Montgomery Clift's debut announcing a new kind of American screen masculinity entirely.

title: Carol
synopsis: Haynes's hushed 1950s New York romance pairs Cate Blanchett's departing housewife with Rooney Mara's shopgirl in a department-store glance that becomes an affair, a custody battle, and one of the most precisely controlled studies of desire ever made — every Edward Lachman frame a Saul Leiter photograph come to life.

title: All About Eve
synopsis: Joseph L. Mankiewicz's razor-tongued Broadway masterpiece introduces aspiring actress Eve Harrington into the inner circle of legend Margo Channing, whose vulnerability Eve exploits with predatory patience — the screenplay, among the most brilliantly written in Hollywood history, earning a record fourteen Academy Award nominations.

title: Sunset Boulevard
synopsis: Billy Wilder's savage anatomy of Hollywood mythology opens on a corpse in a Sunset Boulevard swimming pool and proceeds in flashback to reveal how once-great silent star Norma Desmond entrapped a cynical screenwriter, Gloria Swanson's fearless performance as a woman unable to distinguish delusion from genius itself a kind of genius.

title: Cinderella
synopsis: Walt Disney's Cinderella — the production that saved the studio from bankruptcy — transforms the archetypal fairy tale through animation of such warmth and grace that it has never been surpassed as the definitive telling, its commercial success reversing years of wartime losses and reigniting the Disney animated feature era.

title: The Big Short
synopsis: McKay's frenetic adaptation of Michael Lewis's 2008 housing-crash book follows four outsider investors who predicted the collapse — Christian Bale's autistic hedge-fund visionary, Steve Carell's rage-driven Mark Baum — using fourth-wall-breaking explainers (Margot Robbie in a bubble bath; Anthony Bourdain in a restaurant) that gamified a financial-system collapse into Best Adapted Screenplay.

title: Singin' in the Rain
synopsis: Stanley Donen and Gene Kelly's incandescent musical transforms Hollywood's traumatic transition to sound into an occasion for pure cinematic joy, Kelly's title number — a man dancing alone in the rain with nothing but a lamppost and a gutter puddle — remaining the single most joyful image in the history of American cinema.

title: High Noon
synopsis: Fred Zinnemann's spare, relentless Western unfolds in near-real time as retiring Marshal Will Kane, abandoned by every townsperson he has protected, waits alone for the noon train and the killers it carries — Gary Cooper's performance of suppressed fear and stubborn duty winning the Academy Award and enduring as cinema's definitive portrait of moral isolation.

title: Roman Holiday
synopsis: William Wyler's enchanting Roman Holiday launches Audrey Hepburn's luminous Princess Ann on a stolen day among Rome's fountains and piazzas, where she falls for a worldly American journalist who knows her secret but keeps it — Hepburn's debut performance winning her the Academy Award and inaugurating one of cinema's most beloved screen presences.

title: Seven Samurai
synopsis: Akira Kurosawa's monumental epic follows a destitute farming village that hires seven wandering samurai to defend its harvest from annual bandits, the film's three-hour breadth encompassing comedy, tragedy, and action sequences so foundational they became the invisible grammar of all action cinema that followed.

title: Rear Window
synopsis: Hitchcock's most formally ingenious thriller confines its wheelchair-bound photographer — and the audience — to a single Greenwich Village courtyard, where his growing conviction that a neighbor has committed murder transforms voyeurism into a meditation on cinema itself, implicating us in the obsession it depicts.

title: White Christmas
synopsis: Michael Curtiz's warmly nostalgic White Christmas pairs Bing Crosby and Danny Kaye as former army entertainers orchestrating a tribute to their beloved general, the film's unabashed sentimentality its defining virtue and the reason it became the highest-grossing musical of the 1950s.

title: East of Eden
synopsis: Elia Kazan's searing Steinbeck adaptation casts James Dean's tormented Cal Trask in a Cain-and-Abel rivalry for his father's love in WWI-era California, Dean's incandescent debut — coiled, magnetic, utterly unlike anything preceding it — announcing not merely a new star but a new conception of what screen performance could be.

title: Lady and the Tramp
synopsis: Disney's first widescreen animated feature follows pampered cocker spaniel Lady as she falls for the roguish stray Tramp, the famous spaghetti-sharing scene beneath the moon becoming the most romantically iconic image in the studio's history and making it the highest-grossing film of 1955.

title: The Ten Commandments
synopsis: Cecil B. DeMille's final and greatest spectacle narrates the life of Moses from birth through his confrontation with Ramesses II, the parting of the Red Sea and Charlton Heston's commanding presence creating a film so popular it briefly held the all-time box office record.

title: The Searchers
synopsis: Ford's austere Texas-frontier elegy follows John Wayne's Civil War veteran Ethan Edwards on a years-long search for his abducted niece, confronting an obsession that stains him even as he carries the film toward one of cinema's most quoted closing shots.

title: The Bridge on the River Kwai
synopsis: David Lean's majestic war epic sends British POWs ordered to build their Japanese captors a railway bridge into a moral paradox — that military honor and competence can slide into complicity — Alec Guinness's devastating Colonel Nicholson anchoring a film that earned seven Academy Awards.

title: Vertigo
synopsis: Hitchcock's most psychologically complex thriller — named the greatest film ever made by 191 international critics in the 2012 Sight and Sound poll — sends Detective Scottie Ferguson's obsessive pursuit of a mysterious woman into a portrait of male desire so dark and accurate that cinema took decades to absorb its implications.

title: Ben-Hur
synopsis: William Wyler's spectacular Ben-Hur follows Jewish prince Judah's years of galley slavery and gladiatorial combat on his path to vengeance, the nine-minute chariot race remaining the most thrilling practical action sequence in cinema history and the film's eleven Academy Awards a record tied but never surpassed.

title: Spartacus
synopsis: Stanley Kubrick's Spartacus follows the Thracian slave whose revolt against the Roman Republic grew from individual defiance into mass uprising — Kirk Douglas's commanding performance anchoring a film that also broke the Hollywood blacklist by crediting the blacklisted Dalton Trumbo.

title: Psycho
synopsis: Hitchcock's most profitable and culturally transformative film follows a secretary on the run who vanishes into a remote motel run by a disturbed young man under his mother's influence, the shower sequence permanently altering cinema's grammar and what audiences believed a studio film was permitted to show.

title: The Apartment
synopsis: Billy Wilder's comedy of corporate complicity and suppressed longing follows a lonely company man who lends his apartment to adulterous executives, only to fall for the elevator operator they exploit — Jack Lemmon and Shirley MacLaine's chemistry so true that the film's five Academy Awards, including Best Picture, felt like recognition.

title: West Side Story
synopsis: Robert Wise and Jerome Robbins's electrifying adaptation of the Bernstein-Sondheim musical sets Romeo and Juliet among rival New York street gangs, the choreography so kinetically alive and the tragedy so inevitable that the film earned ten Academy Awards — the most for any musical in history.

title: Lawrence of Arabia
synopsis: David Lean's Lawrence of Arabia traces T.E. Lawrence's transformation from eccentric British officer to desert warrior-mystic through Peter O'Toole's career-defining performance, the film's vast Jordanian landscapes photographed in images so beautiful they constitute their own argument for cinema.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
synopsis: Robert Mulligan's To Kill a Mockingbird captures Harper Lee's Depression-era Alabama through young Scout's eyes as her father Atticus defends a Black man falsely accused of assault, Gregory Peck's embodiment of principled decency winning the Academy Award and producing one of American cinema's most enduring portraits of moral courage.

title: The Wild Bunch
synopsis: Peckinpah's elegiac, blood-splattered revisionist Western tracks an aging outlaw gang attempting one last robbery on the 1913 Mexico–US border, the slow-motion violence and end-of-an-era fatalism rewriting what a Hollywood action film could be.

title: Dr. Strangelove
synopsis: Kubrick's Dr. Strangelove transforms the genuine terror of nuclear annihilation into savage comedy, Peter Sellers's three performances and the film's central joke — that the men in charge are as absurd as the weapons they control — growing more accurate with every passing decade.

title: Mary Poppins
synopsis: Robert Stevenson's Mary Poppins brings P.L. Travers's magical nanny to the screen through Walt Disney's most technically and emotionally ambitious production, Julie Andrews's luminous debut winning the Academy Award and the film becoming the highest-grossing release of 1964.

title: The Sound of Music
synopsis: Robert Wise's Sound of Music transforms the Von Trapp family's flight from Nazi Austria into a celebration of music, faith, and landscape through Julie Andrews's incandescent performance, becoming not merely the highest-grossing musical in history at the time but a cultural institution that has never relinquished its hold.

title: Lady Bird
synopsis: Gerwig's solo-directorial debut places Saoirse Ronan's self-anointed Lady Bird inside a particular Sacramento Catholic-school senior year, her clashing love-and-war with Laurie Metcalf's mother carrying a film whose specificity — pink walls, "Cry Me a River," East-Coast escape — generalizes into one of the great American coming-of-age portraits.

title: Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?
synopsis: Mike Nichols's Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf confines Richard Burton and Elizabeth Taylor's warring academic couple and their hapless guests to a single savage night of drinking and psychic destruction, Taylor's ferocious performance winning the Academy Award for a film of such unsparing intelligence it earned five Oscar nominations.

title: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
synopsis: Sergio Leone's The Good, the Bad and the Ugly sends three gunslingers across Civil War carnage in pursuit of buried Confederate gold, Ennio Morricone's score and Leone's monumental compositions creating the Western as operatic art form.

title: Bonnie and Clyde
synopsis: Arthur Penn's Bonnie and Clyde electrified and divided American cinema by glamorizing its Depression-era bank-robbing couple in Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway's magnetic performances, the film's climactic ambush — balletic, horrifying, beautiful — announcing that Hollywood had definitively broken with the Production Code.

title: The Graduate
synopsis: Mike Nichols's The Graduate sends Dustin Hoffman's blank-faced Benjamin Braddock from seduction by Mrs. Robinson to desperate pursuit of her daughter, Simon and Garfunkel's score elevating the comedy's existential directionlessness into a generational portrait so accurate the 1960s never fully recovered.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
synopsis: Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey traces human evolution from ape-bone to orbiting spacecraft to transcendent rebirth through imagery and music so purely cinematic that it requires no dialogue to communicate its argument — that technology and consciousness are locked in a cycle of creation and obsolescence without discernible end.

title: Funny Girl
synopsis: William Wyler's Funny Girl launches Barbra Streisand from Broadway legend to screen superstar in her film debut as Fanny Brice, Streisand inhabiting the comic genius and romantic anguish so completely that she shared the Academy Award for Best Actress in the first tie in Oscar history.

title: Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid
synopsis: George Roy Hill's Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid follows Paul Newman and Robert Redford's legendary outlaws through the twilight of the American West with such charm, wit, and melancholy that the film transcended its genre to become a permanent American mythology — and the highest-grossing film of 1969.

title: Love Story
synopsis: Arthur Hiller's Love Story offers its doomed Harvard romance between wealthy Oliver Barrett and working-class Jenny Cavilleri without irony or apology, Ali MacGraw and Ryan O'Neal's chemistry generating one of cinema's most improbable critical and commercial phenomena — the fifth-highest-grossing film ever at its release.

title: Patton
synopsis: Franklin Schaffner's Patton opens with George C. Scott's general haranguing unseen troops before the stars and stripes and never surrenders the audacity of that image, the film's portrait of an irreplaceable military genius whose self-mythology made him simultaneously indispensable and impossible winning seven Academy Awards.

title: The French Connection
synopsis: William Friedkin's The French Connection follows Gene Hackman's obsessive NYPD detective through a massive heroin smuggling operation, the car-chase sequence shot through actual Brooklyn traffic establishing a new benchmark for action realism and the Best Picture Oscar announcing that uncompromising American realism had arrived.

title: The Godfather
synopsis: Francis Ford Coppola's operatic portrait of the Corleone crime dynasty traces the corruption of the American immigrant dream through Brando's quietly devastating patriarch and Pacino's transformation from reluctant civilian to ruthless heir, remaining the most commercially successful and critically revered American film ever made.

title: Mean Streets
synopsis: Scorsese's breakthrough turns Little Italy into a moral pressure cooker as Harvey Keitel's Charlie navigates the gap between Catholic conscience and Mafia debt, dragged downward by Robert De Niro's incendiary Johnny Boy in a film whose vintage-pop soundtrack rewrote what movie music could do.

title: The Exorcist
synopsis: William Friedkin's Exorcist transforms the possession of twelve-year-old Regan MacNeil into an inquiry into the limits of modern rationalism, Linda Blair's performance and the film's unsparing physical horror so effectively disturbing that it remains the highest-grossing horror film of all time when adjusted for inflation.

title: American Graffiti
synopsis: George Lucas's American Graffiti freezes a single night in 1962 Modesto — teenagers cruising, flirting, drag-racing under the shadow of Vietnam and adulthood — with such atmospheric precision that it both invented the nostalgia genre and transcended it, launching the careers of Harrison Ford and its director.

title: The Godfather Part II
synopsis: The Godfather Part II achieves the near-impossible by surpassing its predecessor, counterpointing Michael Corleone's moral dissolution in the 1950s against De Niro's luminous portrait of young Vito's immigrant rise, the film's devastating final image of Michael alone at the lake house constituting its own moral verdict.

title: Chinatown
synopsis: Polanski's Chinatown sends Jack Nicholson's Jake Gittes through a Los Angeles water conspiracy of such labyrinthine corruption that the film — Robert Towne's screenplay voted the greatest ever written — functions as both perfect neo-noir and a philosophical argument that institutional evil is finally unreformable.

title: Jaws
synopsis: Spielberg's Jaws inaugurated the summer blockbuster with such force that it permanently restructured the Hollywood economy, Robert Shaw's Indianapolis monologue providing a moment of haunting historical poetry amid the entertainment that dethroned Gone with the Wind as the all-time domestic box office champion.

title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
synopsis: Milos Forman's One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest follows R.P. McMurphy's collision with Nurse Ratched's totalitarian order in a psychiatric institution, Jack Nicholson's incandescent performance and the film's anatomy of institutional power earning a clean sweep of the five major Academy Awards.

title: Rocky
synopsis: John G. Avildsen's Rocky follows the unlikely ascent of Philadelphia club fighter Rocky Balboa from obscurity to a title shot, Sylvester Stallone's performance — which he wrote himself — embodying an optimism so genuine and expertly calibrated that the film won Best Picture and became a permanent American myth.

title: Taxi Driver
synopsis: Scorsese's Taxi Driver follows Travis Bickle's descent through insomniac Manhattan into messianic violence, De Niro's performance sealed inside its own perception so completely that delusion and heroism become indistinguishable — the You talkin to me mirror scene a shorthand for solipsistic American grandiosity the culture has never fully processed.

title: Star Wars
synopsis: George Lucas's Star Wars resurrected the adventure serial as mythological epic, giving Luke Skywalker's journey from Tatooine farm boy to Rebel hero the structural clarity of Joseph Campbell and the visual invention of a decade of cinematic imagination, the film's cultural impact so total it divided cinema history into before and after.

title: Annie Hall
synopsis: Woody Allen's Annie Hall reinvents the romantic comedy through formally audacious reflexivity — direct address, flashbacks, split screens — as Alvy Singer dissects the relationship that ended anyway, Diane Keaton's Oscar-winning performance inaugurating a fashion influence that outlasted the film's many imitators.

title: Saturday Night Fever
synopsis: John Badham's Saturday Night Fever follows Brooklyn teenager Tony Manero's escape from dead-end reality onto the disco floor, John Travolta's magnetic physicality and the Bee Gees' score creating both a star and a cultural moment, the film's unexpectedly dark portrait of working-class masculinity giving the phenomenon its artistic weight.

title: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
synopsis: Spielberg's Close Encounters of the Third Kind follows Roy Neary's obsessive pull toward Devil's Tower after a UFO encounter, the film's climactic communication sequence — humanity's first conversation with the cosmos conducted through color and music — among the most quietly magnificent conclusions in American cinema.

title: The Florida Project
synopsis: Baker's exuberant-and-devastating portrait of a six-year-old (Brooklynn Prince) and her young, unraveling mother (Bria Vinaite) living week-to-week in a lavender-painted budget motel a mile from Disney World — Willem Dafoe's motel-manager Bobby anchoring a film whose tenderness toward American poverty is matched only by its furious refusal to look away.

title: The Deer Hunter
synopsis: Michael Cimino's Deer Hunter follows Pennsylvania steelworkers from their close-knit community into the nightmare of Vietnam and the wreckage it made of their return, the Russian roulette sequences achieving a traumatic power that remains unrepeated and the film's five Academy Awards confirming a new seriousness in American popular cinema.

title: Kramer vs. Kramer
synopsis: Robert Benton's Kramer vs. Kramer follows Manhattan executive Ted Kramer's transformation from negligent husband into devoted father after his wife's departure, Dustin Hoffman and Meryl Streep's performances — the latter's ten minutes of screen time earning her first Oscar — generating the most emotionally precise divorce film ever made.

title: The Empire Strikes Back
synopsis: Irvin Kershner's Empire Strikes Back deepens Lucas's mythology with the revelation that transforms Luke's heroic journey into something far darker, Yoda and the carbon-freezing chamber and the Vader disclosure combining to produce not merely the finest entry in the franchise but one of the great middle chapters in all of narrative cinema.

title: Raging Bull
synopsis: Martin Scorsese's Raging Bull traces Jake LaMotta's rise and self-destruction through Robert De Niro's total physical and psychological transformation, Thelma Schoonmaker's editing and Michael Chapman's black-and-white cinematography giving the brutality of the boxing sequences the visual grammar of Expressionist art.

title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
synopsis: Steven Spielberg's Raiders of the Lost Ark sends Harrison Ford's archaeologist-adventurer across 1930s Cairo and the Egyptian desert in pursuit of the biblical Ark, the film's combination of serial-adventure nostalgia and genuine filmmaking craft producing the defining action-entertainment of its decade.

title: On Golden Pond
synopsis: Mark Rydell's On Golden Pond brings Henry Fonda and Katharine Hepburn together as an aging couple spending their final summer at a New Hampshire lake, Fonda's last performance — a man confronting mortality with characteristic stubbornness — earning him the Academy Award weeks before his death.

title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
synopsis: Spielberg's E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial follows young Elliott's secret friendship with a stranded alien in the California suburbs, the film's Spielbergian mastery of the child's-eye view producing the highest-grossing film in history at the time of its release and a portrait of childhood wonder so accurate it made adults mourn what they had lost.

title: Tootsie
synopsis: Sydney Pollack's Tootsie follows Dustin Hoffman's unemployable actor who disguises himself as a woman to land a soap opera role and inadvertently becomes a feminist icon, the comedy's genuine intelligence about gender and performance elevating what might have been farce into one of the finest American films of the decade.

title: Terms of Endearment
synopsis: James L. Brooks's Terms of Endearment traces the relationship between Aurora Greenway and her daughter Emma across decades of accommodation and love, Shirley MacLaine and Debra Winger's performances so lived-in and Jack Nicholson's Garrett Breedlove so magnificently comic that the film's five Academy Awards felt like recognition rather than achievement.

title: Ghostbusters
synopsis: Ivan Reitman's Ghostbusters deploys Bill Murray, Dan Aykroyd, and Harold Ramis as parapsychology professors turned ghost-exterminators with such comic precision and infectious delight in its own premise that the film became the highest-grossing comedy in history at the time of release.

title: Beverly Hills Cop
synopsis: Martin Brest's Beverly Hills Cop sends Eddie Murphy's Detroit detective Axel Foley into the immaculate gardens of Beverly Hills to investigate his friend's murder, Murphy's improvisational genius and the film's comic friction between street instinct and manicured privilege producing the highest-grossing comedy of 1984.

title: Amadeus
synopsis: Milos Forman's Amadeus tells the story of Mozart's genius and Salieri's torment not as biography but as theological argument — if God chose to speak through Mozart's beauty and vulgarity, what does that imply about God? — F. Murray Abraham's Salieri the most compelling witness in cinema to both transcendence and its costs.

title: Back to the Future
synopsis: Robert Zemeckis's Back to the Future sends Michael J. Fox's Marty McFly from 1985 to 1955 in a DeLorean time machine, the film's clockwork plotting — every detail paying off exactly when required — producing the most mechanically perfect blockbuster comedy of the decade and the highest-grossing film of 1985.

title: Platoon
synopsis: Oliver Stone's Platoon places Charlie Sheen's idealistic volunteer in the moral nightmare of Vietnam between two sergeants — Willem Dafoe's humanist Elias and Tom Berenger's brutal Barnes — the film's autobiographical fury and four Academy Awards confirming it as the definitive American reckoning with the war.

title: Come and See
synopsis: Klimov's shattering Belarusian-front anti-war film follows a teenage partisan, Flyora, as he witnesses Nazi atrocities first-hand — a relentless first-person descent through corpse-strewn forests and a village massacre staged with documentary literalness that has been called the most devastating film about anything ever made.

title: Full Metal Jacket
synopsis: Kubrick's Full Metal Jacket splits across the dehumanizing hell of Parris Island and the street combat of Hue City, R. Lee Ermey's Sergeant Hartman — a performance so authentic Kubrick cast an actual Marine drill instructor — embodying the industrial system that transforms men into killing instruments without remainder.

title: Fatal Attraction
synopsis: Adrian Lyne's Fatal Attraction forces a happily married man's one-night stand with Glenn Close's Alex Forrest into a sustained examination of bourgeois domestic terror, Close's refusal to let her character be merely monstrous elevating the film above its thriller mechanics into something genuinely disturbing about desire and consequence.

title: Rain Man
synopsis: Barry Levinson's Rain Man pairs Dustin Hoffman's autistic savant Raymond with Tom Cruise's self-centered Charlie in a cross-country drive that transforms their relationship through patient comic accumulation, Hoffman's scrupulously researched performance winning the Academy Award and permanently altering public understanding of autism.

title: Die Hard
synopsis: John McTiernan's Die Hard traps New York detective John McClane barefoot in a Nakatomi Plaza seized by Hans Gruber's thieves, Bruce Willis's everyman hero and Alan Rickman's magnificent villain together defining the action film's template so comprehensively that the following decade's output is largely a series of variations.

title: When Harry Met Sally...
synopsis: Rob Reiner's When Harry Met Sally follows Nora Ephron's argument — that men and women cannot be friends — across twelve years of Billy Crystal and Meg Ryan's relationship with such wit and fidelity to how romantic feeling actually develops that the film redefined the romantic comedy permanently.

title: Batman
synopsis: Tim Burton's Batman translates the DC hero to the gothic Gotham of his imagination, Michael Keaton's quietly strange Bruce Wayne meeting his match in Jack Nicholson's operatically scenery-devouring Joker — the film's visual design so definitive that it established the aesthetic template for the superhero film's commercial dominance.

title: Close-Up
synopsis: Kiarostami's revolutionary docufiction reconstructs a real Iranian fraud case — a film-loving unemployed man impersonates the director Mohsen Makhmalbaf to convince a wealthy Tehran family they will star in his next picture — restaging the trial and the deception with the actual people playing themselves, dissolving the wall between document and drama.

title: Dances with Wolves
synopsis: Kevin Costner's Dances with Wolves follows a Union officer's gradual immersion into and adoption by a Lakota Sioux community, the film's genuine respect for its indigenous subject and its epic landscapes earning seven Academy Awards and reviving the Western as a vehicle for moral seriousness.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
synopsis: Jonathan Demme's Silence of the Lambs sends FBI trainee Clarice Starling into the underground cell of Hannibal Lecter to catch another killer, Jodie Foster's performance of intelligence and self-possession and Anthony Hopkins's sixteen minutes of screen time earning the film a clean sweep of all five major Academy Awards.

title: Terminator 2: Judgment Day
synopsis: James Cameron's Terminator 2 sends the same T-800 model that hunted Sarah Connor back in time as John's protector, the film's then-unprecedented CGI liquid-metal villain and Linda Hamilton's physical transformation into a warrior mother producing a sequel that surpassed its already perfect original.

title: Unforgiven
synopsis: Clint Eastwood's Unforgiven sends retired outlaw William Munny on one last job as a bounty hunter, the film's methodical dismantling of Western mythology — every act of violence carrying genuine consequence, every heroic pose exposed as performance — earning four Academy Awards and standing as the genre's most intelligent self-examination.

title: Jurassic Park
synopsis: Steven Spielberg's Jurassic Park resurrects the dinosaur through Stan Winston's animatronics and nascent CGI, the brachiosaurus's first appearance one of cinema's great revelation moments and the film's central argument — that the hubris of recreating life without wisdom is its own inevitable punishment — delivered with uncommon narrative intelligence.

title: Schindler's List
synopsis: Spielberg's Schindler's List follows German industrialist Oskar Schindler's transformation from opportunistic profiteer to reluctant savior of over a thousand Jewish workers, Janusz Kaminski's black-and-white cinematography and the single red coat worn by a child producing images of moral weight so severe the film has become a permanent part of Holocaust memory.

title: The Lion King
synopsis: The Lion King sends lion prince Simba into exile after his uncle Scar engineers his father Mufasa's murder, the film's Shakespearean gravity and Hans Zimmer's score combining with extraordinary voice performances to produce Disney's masterpiece and the highest-grossing traditionally animated film in history.

title: Pulp Fiction
synopsis: Tarantino's Pulp Fiction weaves three interlocking Los Angeles crime stories through a non-linear structure that made its wit and violence feel simultaneously new and classical, the Palme d'Or and seven Academy Award nominations confirming that postmodern pastiche had become the defining mode of American cinema.

title: Forrest Gump
synopsis: Robert Zemeckis's Forrest Gump follows its title character through four decades of American history with a tonal precision that renders innocence as reproach, Tom Hanks's performance achieving genuine difficulty in making sincerity legible without condescension and earning the film Best Picture.

title: The Shawshank Redemption
synopsis: Frank Darabont's Shawshank Redemption follows Andy Dufresne through nineteen years of wrongful imprisonment, his survival requiring a kind of inward freedom the institution is designed to extinguish, Morgan Freeman's narration of patient wisdom transforming a prison story into cinema's most beloved fable about hope.

title: Braveheart
synopsis: Mel Gibson's Braveheart sends William Wallace's outnumbered Scottish forces against English tyranny with a grandeur and ferocity that earned five Academy Awards and sparked a wave of Scottish national pride, its genuine mythological ambition producing a historical spectacle of rare emotional force.

title: Toy Story
synopsis: John Lasseter's Toy Story launches the computer-animated feature film with a story of genuine emotional intelligence — Woody's terror at obsolescence, Buzz's dawning self-knowledge — the film's seamless integration of technological novelty and narrative craft producing not merely Pixar's first feature but the template for everything it would achieve.

title: Titanic
synopsis: James Cameron's Titanic entwines Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet's fictional romance across the three days of the ship's voyage and sinking, the film's understanding that disaster movies are fundamentally love stories giving its spectacle an emotional weight that earned eleven Academy Awards and made it the highest-grossing film in history.

title: Saving Private Ryan
synopsis: Spielberg's Saving Private Ryan opens with twenty-four minutes of D-Day carnage so viscerally accurate that veterans wept and left cinemas, the subsequent mission to retrieve one paratrooper earning five Academy Awards and permanently altering cinema's grammar for depicting the moral experience of combat.

title: American Beauty
synopsis: Sam Mendes's American Beauty follows Lester Burnham's mid-life disintegration in a Saran-wrapped suburb with satirical precision that earned five Academy Awards, Kevin Spacey's performance of a man discovering freedom through annihilation and Conrad Hall's crimson-rose cinematography defining late-century American cinema's most powerful aesthetic.

title: Gladiator
synopsis: Ridley Scott's Gladiator sends Roman general Maximus from betrayal into slavery and the arena, Russell Crowe's physical authority and Joaquin Phoenix's exquisitely malevolent Commodus powering a historical epic that revived the toga film, earned five Academy Awards, and gave the 2000s its foundational action-adventure template.

title: Cast Away
synopsis: Robert Zemeckis's Cast Away strips Tom Hanks's FedEx engineer of everything human except intelligence and will on a Pacific island, Hanks's monologue-free performance — four years of physical and psychological isolation communicated entirely through behavior — producing the purest acting showcase since Robinson Crusoe entered the cultural imagination.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
synopsis: Peter Jackson's Fellowship of the Ring translates Tolkien's world into cinematic reality through a production of such sustained ambition that the mythology found its definitive visual form, earning four Academy Awards and announcing that fantasy could achieve the grandeur of the best historical epic.

title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
synopsis: Chris Columbus's Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone introduces Daniel Radcliffe's orphaned wizard to Hogwarts with a fidelity to Rowling's world and an atmospheric richness that launched the most commercially successful film franchise in history, the film's visual invention becoming part of a generation's imaginative furniture.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
synopsis: Peter Jackson's The Two Towers advances the War of the Ring on three fronts — including Andy Serkis's motion-capture Gollum, the first photorealistic digital character in cinema history — the Battle of Helm's Deep sustaining forty minutes of tactical combat at a narrative intensity no subsequent film has equaled.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
synopsis: Peter Jackson's The Return of the King brings three years of filmmaking to a conclusion of such emotional magnitude that it swept all eleven of its Academy Award nominations — the most ever won by a single film without a single loss — confirming the trilogy as the supreme achievement of the digital era.

title: Finding Nemo
synopsis: Andrew Stanton's Finding Nemo follows overprotective clownfish Marlin across the ocean in search of his captured son, the film's visual beauty and genuine paternal emotion producing the studio's most beloved work and then the highest-grossing animated film in history.

title: Million Dollar Baby
synopsis: Clint Eastwood's Million Dollar Baby traces the partnership between hardened trainer Frankie Dunn and tenacious unknown Maggie Fitzgerald, Hilary Swank's physical and emotional commitment and Morgan Freeman's quiet moral authority earning four Academy Awards in a film whose severity the studio tried to prevent.

title: Brokeback Mountain
synopsis: Ang Lee's Brokeback Mountain follows Wyoming ranch hands Ennis Del Mar and Jack Twist through twenty years of suppressed love conducted in brief mountain reunions, Heath Ledger's performance of anguished internalized feeling and the film's three Academy Awards making it the most beautiful and heartbreaking American romance of its decade.

title: The Departed
synopsis: Martin Scorsese's The Departed sends Leonardo DiCaprio's undercover cop and Matt Damon's police mole spiraling toward each other in an Irish-American Boston mob saga, Jack Nicholson's Frank Costello the most operatically menacing presence in the director's crime filmography and the film's four Academy Awards a career overdue recognition.

title: The Dark Knight
synopsis: Christopher Nolan's Dark Knight transforms the superhero film into a crime epic of Shakespearean moral ambiguity, Heath Ledger's Joker — a portrait of anarchic intelligence delivered with total physical commitment that earned a posthumous Academy Award — permanently demonstrating that the form was capable of genuine moral seriousness without sacrificing commercial power.

title: Slumdog Millionaire
synopsis: Danny Boyle's Slumdog Millionaire follows Mumbai orphan Jamal through the flashback structure of a quiz show investigation, each question answered through a biographical trauma, the film's kinetic energy and Dev Patel's performance earning eight Academy Awards.

title: Wall-E
synopsis: Andrew Stanton's WALL-E opens on a future Earth buried under consumer waste and follows a small garbage-compacting robot whose seven hundred years of solitary work have made him something approaching human — the first, nearly silent half the most purely cinematic storytelling Pixar has achieved.

title: Avatar
synopsis: James Cameron's Avatar deploys the then-most-advanced CGI in cinema history to construct the world of Pandora, where a Marine-turned-Na'vi discovers through immersion in another civilization the bankruptcy of the colonial logic that sent him there — the film's visual invention earning three Academy Awards and making it the highest-grossing film in history.

title: Toy Story 3
synopsis: Lee Unkrich's Toy Story 3 sends Woody, Buzz, and the gang to a daycare center that proves to be a prison, the film's climax at the furnace achieving genuine terror rare in animated cinema before resolving into a farewell to childhood so emotionally precise that it devastated audiences who had grown up with the original.

title: Inception
synopsis: Christopher Nolan's Inception sends Leonardo DiCaprio's dream-thief through layered subconscious architectures on a corporate espionage mission that becomes an examination of grief, guilt, and the impossibility of knowing whether what we experience is real — the film's visual grammar of collapsing cities generating the decade's most discussed ending.

title: The King's Speech
synopsis: Tom Hooper's King's Speech traces King George VI's partnership with Australian speech therapist Lionel Logue as he works to overcome his crippling stammer before WWII, Colin Firth's embodiment of royal vulnerability and Geoffrey Rush's unorthodox warmth earning four Academy Awards and producing one of cinema's finest portraits of friendship across class.

title: Argo
synopsis: Ben Affleck's Argo dramatizes the 1980 CIA-Canadian operation that rescued six American diplomats from Tehran using a fake science fiction film production as cover, the combination of genuine historical tension and dry comedy about Hollywood's self-importance earning three Academy Awards including Best Picture.

title: 12 Years a Slave
synopsis: Steve McQueen's 12 Years a Slave follows free Black man Solomon Northup through the seven years of his Louisiana enslavement with an unflinching refusal to aestheticize suffering, Chiwetel Ejiofor's performance of sustained dignity and Lupita Nyong'o's Oscar-winning portrait of Patsey making it the most morally necessary American film of its decade.

title: Boyhood
synopsis: Richard Linklater's Boyhood films Mason Evans Jr. from age six to eighteen using the same actors across twelve years of actual production, the film's temporal audacity transforming the ordinary accumulation of childhood into something no montage or makeup could replicate — Patricia Arquette's everyday heroism earning her the Academy Award.

title: The Revenant
synopsis: Alejandro Gonzalez Inarritu's Revenant sends Hugh Glass across winter wilderness after a bear mauling and his son's murder, Emmanuel Lubezki's natural-light cinematography producing images of savage beauty that earned two Academy Awards and Leonardo DiCaprio the long-delayed Best Actor recognition for a performance of total physical commitment.

title: Mad Max: Fury Road
synopsis: George Miller's Mad Max: Fury Road conducts a two-hour high-octane chase across post-apocalyptic desert with the fury and precision of a symphony, Charlize Theron's Imperator Furiosa — one arm, unbreakable will — challenging Tom Hardy's Max for the film's moral center while Miller deploys practical stunt work at a scale that made the film's six Academy Awards inevitable.

title: The Force Awakens
synopsis: J.J. Abrams's The Force Awakens resurrects the Star Wars mythology thirty years after the Empire's defeat through Daisy Ridley's Rey and John Boyega's Finn, the film's fidelity to the original trilogy's emotional register and the return of Harrison Ford's Han Solo producing the largest opening weekend in cinema history.

title: Moonlight
synopsis: Barry Jenkins's Moonlight follows Chiron through three chapters of his Miami life with a visual delicacy that made it the most aesthetically refined Best Picture winner in a generation and a landmark in Black and LGBTQ+ cinema, Mahershala Ali's Academy Award-winning performance of surrogate paternity its most precisely moving element.

title: La La Land
synopsis: Damien Chazelle's La La Land follows aspiring actress Mia and jazz pianist Sebastian through a Los Angeles romance calibrated to the exact tension between love and ambition, Emma Stone's Oscar-winning performance and Justin Hurwitz's score producing a musical that mourns what it celebrates — the dream pursued at the cost of the life that might have been.

title: Get Out
synopsis: Jordan Peele's Get Out sends Daniel Kaluuya's Black photographer to his white girlfriend's family estate and into a horror that is simultaneously supernatural and precisely social — the Armitage family's liberal racism more disturbing than their secret — the film's allegorical intelligence making it the most important American genre film of its decade.

title: Avengers: Endgame
synopsis: Anthony and Joe Russo's Avengers: Endgame resolves the decade-long Marvel narrative through a climax of genuine emotional resonance, Tony Stark's sacrifice and Steve Rogers's earned rest producing a conclusion to the most ambitious multi-film storytelling project in Hollywood history that became the highest-grossing film ever made.

title: Parasite
synopsis: Bong Joon-ho's Parasite follows the Kim family's infiltration of the wealthy Park household through elaborate deceptions, the film's first half operating as caper comedy before a basement revelation shifts it into something darker and stranger, its four Academy Awards including the first Best Picture for a non-English-language film confirming world cinema had found its global audience.

title: Nomadland
synopsis: Chloe Zhao's Nomadland follows Fern, a woman in her sixties who lost everything in the Great Recession, through the van-dwelling communities of the American West, Frances McDormand's performance of dignity and solitude earning her third Academy Award and Zhao becoming only the second woman to win Best Director.

title: Dune
synopsis: Denis Villeneuve's Dune Part One translates the first half of Frank Herbert's near-untranslatable novel into a film of sustained visual grandeur, Timothee Chalamet's Paul Atreides and Zendaya's Chani orbiting each other across Arrakeen landscapes that Greig Fraser's Oscar-winning cinematography renders as both alien and mythological.

title: Top Gun: Maverick
synopsis: Joseph Kosinski's Top Gun: Maverick sends Tom Cruise's aging pilot back to train the next generation for a mission his instincts and experience are uniquely suited to execute, the combination of genuine aerial photography and emotional closure making it the year's highest-grossing film and a rare blockbuster that surpassed its original.

title: Everything Everywhere All at Once
synopsis: Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert's Everything Everywhere All at Once follows a failing laundromat owner through a multiverse crisis only she can resolve, Michelle Yeoh's performance and the film's audacity earning seven Academy Awards including Best Picture — Ke Huy Quan's comeback, Yeoh's historic first Best Actress for an Asian woman.

title: Oppenheimer
synopsis: Christopher Nolan's Oppenheimer traces the creation and detonation of the atomic bomb through Cillian Murphy's haunted J. Robert Oppenheimer, the film's formal ambition earning seven Academy Awards and making it the highest-grossing biopic in history.

title: Barbie
synopsis: Greta Gerwig's Barbie follows Margot Robbie's Barbieland resident into the real world where the film's satirical intelligence about feminism and patriarchy accumulates beneath its pink surface until America Ferrera's monologue makes the argument explicit, the film becoming the highest-grossing release of 2023.

title: Killers of the Flower Moon
synopsis: Martin Scorsese's Killers of the Flower Moon traces the systematic murder of the Osage Nation after oil was discovered beneath their Oklahoma land, Robert De Niro's William Hale and Leonardo DiCaprio's Ernest Burkhart embodying the insidious complicity of ordinary evil while Lily Gladstone's Mollie — watching everything — becomes the film's moral center.

title: Poor Things
synopsis: Yorgos Lanthimos's Poor Things sends Emma Stone's reanimated Bella Baxter on a journey of bodily and philosophical self-discovery whose anarchic rejection of Victorian propriety earned Stone the Academy Award and the film the Venice Golden Lion.

title: Dune: Part Two
synopsis: Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part Two sends Paul Atreides among the Fremen as Chani's skepticism and Paul's messianic momentum reach their terrible convergence, Austin Butler's Feyd-Rautha providing the film's most stylized performance and Hans Zimmer's score amplifying the tragedy of a man choosing myth over love.

title: The Substance
synopsis: Coralie Fargeat's Substance follows Demi Moore's fading celebrity through a body-horror parable about the entertainment industry's consumption of women, the film's escalating grotesquerie earning Fargeat the Cannes Best Screenplay award and Moore her first major awards recognition in two decades.

title: Rebecca
synopsis: Hitchcock's Rebecca follows the unnamed second Mrs. de Winter through Manderley's haunted grandeur, Joan Fontaine's performance of vulnerability and Judith Anderson's magnificent Mrs. Danvers — the greatest housekeeper in cinema — creating an atmosphere of psychological menace that earned the film Best Picture and remains the definitive adaptation of du Maurier's novel.

title: The Philadelphia Story
synopsis: George Cukor's Philadelphia Story sends Cary Grant's charming ex-husband and Jimmy Stewart's tabloid reporter to complicate Katharine Hepburn's patrician wedding plans, the film's brilliant comic machinery and the chemistry of three of Hollywood's finest actors at peak form earning Stewart the Academy Award and Hepburn her greatest comedic triumph.

title: Citizen Kane
synopsis: Orson Welles's Citizen Kane follows reporters investigating the meaning of Charles Foster Kane's dying word Rosebud through flashbacks assembling a portrait of a man whose ambition for love expressed itself as the desire for power, the film's technical innovations so comprehensive that it effectively invented the visual grammar of modern cinema.

title: How Green Was My Valley
synopsis: John Ford's How Green Was My Valley follows young Huw Morgan's coming-of-age in a Welsh coal-mining community as industrialization and emigration slowly dismantle everything his family has been, a film of such emotional directness that its Best Picture win over Citizen Kane remains cinema's most discussed upset.

title: Casablanca
synopsis: Michael Curtiz's Casablanca, the most beloved film Hollywood has ever produced, follows Rick Blaine's impossible choice between the love of his life and the cause he abandoned, Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman's chemistry generating cinema's definitive portrait of sacrifice as its own form of dignity.

title: Double Indemnity
synopsis: Billy Wilder's Double Indemnity sends insurance salesman Walter Neff into Barbara Stanwyck's trap with the inevitability of Greek tragedy, the film's ruthless intelligence about desire as self-destruction and Edward G. Robinson's Barton Keyes making it the template for every morally compromised thriller that followed.

title: Going My Way
synopsis: Leo McCarey's Going My Way follows young Father O'Malley's arrival at a struggling New York parish alongside the elderly Father Fitzgibbon, Bing Crosby's easy warmth and the film's unsentimental examination of institutional change earning seven Academy Awards — more than any film since the ceremony's inception.

title: Laura
synopsis: Otto Preminger's Laura follows detective Mark McPherson's investigation into the apparent murder of a young advertising executive, Gene Tierney's portrait and Dana Andrews's growing obsession creating the most stylishly melancholic mystery in American cinema, David Raksin's score becoming one of the most imitated in film history.

title: Rashomon
synopsis: Akira Kurosawa's Rashomon presents the same violent encounter in the forest through four contradictory accounts, the film's formal argument — that subjective truth is all we possess and self-serving narrative the condition of human consciousness — introducing Japanese cinema to the world and permanently enriching cinema's philosophical vocabulary.

title: A Streetcar Named Desire
synopsis: Elia Kazan's A Streetcar Named Desire brings Tennessee Williams's shattering play to the screen through Vivien Leigh's Blanche DuBois and Marlon Brando's Stanley Kowalski, the collision between Southern fantasy and brute modernity earning four Academy Awards and establishing Brando's Method as the dominant force in American screen acting.

title: Stalag 17
synopsis: Billy Wilder's Stalag 17 sends William Holden's cynical, self-interested Sefton into a POW camp where someone is betraying escape plans to the Germans, the film's combination of comedy and genuine suspense earning Holden the Academy Award and demonstrating Wilder's unique capacity to find darkness inside entertainment.

title: From Here to Eternity
synopsis: Fred Zinnemann's From Here to Eternity follows Army personnel at Pearl Harbor in the months before the Japanese attack, Montgomery Clift, Burt Lancaster, and Frank Sinatra — in the comeback role that saved his career — together producing a film of sustained intensity that earned eight Academy Awards.

title: On the Waterfront
synopsis: Elia Kazan's On the Waterfront sends Marlon Brando's broken-down boxer Terry Malloy into a confrontation with union corruption he has facilitated, the I coulda been a contender speech and the film's moral urgency earning eight Academy Awards and Brando's first Oscar.

title: Witness for the Prosecution
synopsis: Billy Wilder's Witness for the Prosecution adapts Agatha Christie's courtroom thriller through Charles Laughton's magnificent barrister Sir Wilfrid Robarts, the film's construction of apparently airtight guilt and its celebrated reversal making it the finest legal drama in cinema.

title: North by Northwest
synopsis: Hitchcock's North by Northwest sends Cary Grant's mistaken-for-a-spy advertising man across America — from the Plaza Hotel to a prairie highway where a crop duster tries to kill him to the faces of Mount Rushmore — in a film of such buoyant comic invention and visual elegance that it constitutes the director's most purely pleasurable achievement.

title: Jules and Jim
synopsis: Francois Truffaut's Jules and Jim traces an equilateral friendship over decades — two men and the free-spirited Catherine whose love they share — Jeanne Moreau's incandescent performance making it the New Wave's most joyful and heartbreaking exploration of the impossibility of sustaining love in its purest form.

title: 8½
synopsis: Fellini's 8 1/2 follows a celebrated director paralyzed by creative emptiness through memory, fantasy, and the claims of the women in his life, Marcello Mastroianni's performance of charming, guilt-ridden evasion making the film the supreme portrait of artistic self-indulgence and the impossible demands that art places on the life that must generate it.

title: My Fair Lady
synopsis: George Cukor's My Fair Lady translates the Lerner and Loewe musical with a visual grandeur and Rex Harrison's linguistic comedy so complete that the film earned eight Academy Awards, Audrey Hepburn's Eliza Doolittle bringing a warmth and physical grace that no stage production had quite achieved.

title: Persona
synopsis: Ingmar Bergman's Persona places a mute actress and her nurse in isolation on a remote island and watches their identities begin to dissolve and merge, the film's formal disruptions matching its inquiry into the impossibility of stable selfhood with a cinematic argument that has generated more critical writing than almost any film ever made.

title: The Battle of Algiers
synopsis: Gillo Pontecorvo's Battle of Algiers reconstructs the 1954-1957 Algerian independence struggle with documentary-like immediacy that makes it impossible to determine which footage is archival and which was staged, the film's refusal to falsify the moral complexity of anti-colonial violence making it the most politically serious war film of the twentieth century.

title: Cool Hand Luke
synopsis: Stuart Rosenberg's Cool Hand Luke follows Paul Newman's anti-authoritarian prisoner through a Florida labor camp where his charismatic resistance to institutional power elevates him to mythology among his fellow inmates, Newman's performance constituting one of cinema's most precise portraits of existential non-conformity.

title: Midnight Cowboy
synopsis: John Schlesinger's Midnight Cowboy follows naive Texas hustler Joe Buck and consumptive con man Ratso Rizzo through the brutal economics of New York survival, Dustin Hoffman and Jon Voight's performances so authentic and the portrait of urban desperation so unsparing that it remains the only X-rated film in history to win Best Picture.

title: A Clockwork Orange
synopsis: Kubrick's A Clockwork Orange follows Alex DeLarge's ultra-violence, imprisonment, and state conditioning through a stylized future Britain with formal precision and Malcolm McDowell's performance of charismatic menace, the film's argument about free will and the violence required to produce social order generating controversy that has never fully subsided.

title: Cabaret
synopsis: Bob Fosse's Cabaret deploys the Berlin cabaret as moral mirror of Weimar Germany's collapse, Liza Minnelli's Sally Bowles and Joel Grey's Master of Ceremonies creating the most unsettling musical in cinema history and earning eight Academy Awards alongside the era's defining portrait of artistic complicity in political catastrophe.

title: Network
synopsis: Sidney Lumet's Network sends anchorman Howard Beale's breakdown across network television, Peter Finch's I'm mad as hell oration becoming the most quoted political speech in cinema history and Faye Dunaway's ratings-obsessed executive embodying a media logic the 21st century proved prophetic rather than satirical.

title: Blade Runner
synopsis: Ridley Scott's Blade Runner sends Harrison Ford's weary detective through a rain-soaked, neon-drenched 2019 Los Angeles where the line between human and replicant dissolves, Rutger Hauer's tears in rain speech — improvised on set — providing one of cinema's most haunting final soliloquies and the film's visual world becoming the founding text of cinematic cyberpunk.

title: Thelma & Louise
synopsis: Ridley Scott's Thelma and Louise sends Susan Sarandon and Geena Davis on a road trip that transforms into an outlaw flight, the film's examination of female self-determination under male violence and its final freeze-frame refusal of capture producing one of American cinema's most debated and enduring conclusions.

title: Malcolm X
synopsis: Spike Lee's Malcolm X traces its subject from street hustler through Nation of Islam minister to global human rights advocate through Denzel Washington's towering performance, the film's three-and-a-half-hour scope justified by the moral enormity of a life that changed the meaning of Black American selfhood.

title: The Piano
synopsis: Jane Campion's The Piano sends Holly Hunter's mute Scottish pianist to colonial New Zealand, where her instrument — traded by her husband, coveted by Harvey Keitel's Baines — becomes the medium through which suppressed desire finds its only expression, the film's Palme d'Or and three Academy Awards confirming Campion as the finest female director in cinema history.

title: Groundhog Day
synopsis: Harold Ramis's Groundhog Day traps weatherman Phil Connors in a single February day in Punxsutawney in what begins as comic nightmare and gradually reveals itself as a philosophical fable about character, transformation, and the conditions under which a human being becomes capable of love — Bill Murray's performance finding the gravity inside the comedy.

title: The Fugitive
synopsis: Andrew Davis's Fugitive sends wrongly convicted surgeon Richard Kimble on a tightly plotted pursuit through Chicago with Tommy Lee Jones's U.S. Marshal Sam Gerard in pursuit, Jones's Academy Award-winning performance of comic authority and the film's relentless momentum making it the finest example of the classical Hollywood chase film.

title: L.A. Confidential
synopsis: Curtis Hanson's L.A. Confidential enters 1950s Los Angeles through three policemen whose separate investigations converge on a conspiracy reaching to the LAPD's highest levels, Kim Basinger's Veronica Lake lookalike and James Ellroy's labyrinthine plotting earning two Academy Awards and producing the finest crime film of the decade.

title: Spirited Away
synopsis: Hayao Miyazaki's Spirited Away sends ten-year-old Chihiro through the spirit world's bath-house economy to rescue her parents, the film's visual invention — No-Face, the radish spirit, the coal creatures — inexhaustible and its examination of labor and identity operating below the surface of a film that earned the Academy Award and became Japan's highest-grossing production.

title: Mulholland Drive
synopsis: David Lynch's Mulholland Drive follows aspiring actress Betty and amnesiac Rita through the dream-logic of Hollywood until the film folds back on itself, the second half retroactively reinterpreting the first as wish-fulfillment — Naomi Watts's dual performance and Lynch's construction of beautiful menace earning him the Cannes Best Director prize.

title: City of God
synopsis: Fernando Meirelles and Katia Lund's City of God traces the evolution of organized crime in Rio de Janeiro's favelas across two decades through the eyes of Rocket, who escapes via photography while his childhood friend rises to violent dominance — the film's kinetic energy and moral honesty making it the most important Brazilian film ever made.

title: The Social Network
synopsis: David Fincher's Social Network dramatizes the founding of Facebook as a study in betrayal, intellectual theft, and the particular loneliness of a man who built the world's largest social network because he didn't know how to make friends, Aaron Sorkin's screenplay earning the Academy Award for a film that understood Silicon Valley's moral psychology before the rest of the culture caught up.

title: The Artist
synopsis: Michel Hazanavicius's The Artist sends silent movie star George Valentin into denial and decline as the talkies arrive, Jean Dujardin's Oscar-winning physical comedy and Berenice Bejo's warmth conducting a love letter to early cinema with such knowing affection that the film earned five Academy Awards and became the only silent film to win Best Picture since Wings in 1927.

title: Gravity
synopsis: Alfonso Cuaron's Gravity strands Sandra Bullock's Mission Specialist Ryan Stone in orbit after debris destroys her shuttle, Emmanuel Lubezki's single-take cinematography achieving a spatial grammar for weightlessness that had never existed before and the film's stripped-down survival story earning seven Academy Awards including Best Director.

title: Her
synopsis: Spike Jonze's Her follows Theodore Twombly's falling in love with Samantha, an AI operating system voiced by Scarlett Johansson, Joaquin Phoenix's achingly sincere performance and a vision of near-future Los Angeles of utopian gentleness arguing that the emotional authenticity of a relationship is independent of its material substrate.

title: Whiplash
synopsis: Damien Chazelle's Whiplash sends Andrew Neiman's drumming ambition into the psychological warfare of J.K. Simmons's Terence Fletcher, the film's examination of the violence required to produce excellence earning five Academy Awards and generating the most intensely debated ending of its decade.

title: The Favourite
synopsis: Yorgos Lanthimos's The Favourite sets three women — Olivia Colman's Queen Anne, Rachel Weisz's Sarah Churchill, and Emma Stone's Abigail Hill — in combat for power in early 18th-century England, Colman's Academy Award-winning performance of damaged, manipulable majesty making it the finest British historical film of its era.

title: The Power of the Dog
synopsis: Jane Campion's Power of the Dog sends Phil Burbank's domineering rancher into a psychosexual confrontation with his brother's new stepson, Benedict Cumberbatch's performance of coiled repression earning Campion the Academy Award and BAFTA — the first woman to win both — and the film's final revelation reframing everything that preceded it.

title: Tár
synopsis: Todd Field's Tar follows the controlled destruction of Lydia Tar through Cate Blanchett's performance of such magnetic authority that the film's formal severity feels like reverence — Blanchett's work considered among the finest screen performances of the century at every major ceremony from Cannes to the Academy.

title: Anora
synopsis: Sean Baker's Anora sends Mikey Madison's Brighton Beach sex worker through a whirlwind Vegas marriage to a Russian oligarch's son and the chaotic Russian envoys dispatched to annul it, the film's Palme d'Or and Best Picture Oscar confirming Baker as American independent cinema's most humane chronicler of the economically precarious.

title: Conclave
synopsis: Edward Berger's Conclave follows Cardinal Lawrence's management of a papal election interrupted by revelations that test his faith and judgment, Ralph Fiennes's performance of intellectual steadiness under mounting pressure making it the finest Vatican drama in cinema.

title: Emilia Pérez
synopsis: Jacques Audiard's Emilia Perez sends Zoe Saldana's cartel lawyer to help a feared Mexican drug lord transition into the woman she has always been, the film's audacious genre hybridization — crime thriller, musical, identity drama — earning five Academy Award nominations for a Spanish-language film by a French director that defied every categorization.

title: I Love Lucy
synopsis: Lucille Ball's I Love Lucy not only defined the American situation comedy but invented the production practices — 35mm film, live studio audience, multiple cameras — that made all subsequent American television possible, Ball's physical genius and the Ricardos' indelible marriage establishing a model of domestic comedy that has never been surpassed.

title: The Twilight Zone
synopsis: Rod Serling's Twilight Zone transforms the anthology format into a vehicle for moral parable and science-fiction allegory, each episode's final twist serving not as mere surprise but as verdict — Serling's weekly argument that the monsters are always us producing the most enduringly influential series in American television history.

title: The Sopranos
synopsis: David Chase's Sopranos inaugurated prestige television drama by applying the moral grammar of the crime film to a New Jersey mob boss in therapy, James Gandolfini's irreplaceable performance communicating the full weight of a man who suspects his own emptiness but cannot stop filling it with violence, and inventing the narrative grammar every subsequent prestige drama has operated within.

title: The Wire
synopsis: David Simon's The Wire constructs its portrait of institutional failure across five Baltimore seasons by giving equal dramatic weight to the police and the men they pursue, its radical refusal to designate heroes or villains making it the most politically serious drama in the history of American television.

title: Breaking Bad
synopsis: Vince Gilligan's Breaking Bad follows Walter White's transformation from cancer-diagnosed chemistry teacher to methamphetamine kingpin with narrative precision so complete that the Guinness World Record for most critically acclaimed television series merely formalizes what audiences understood instinctively: nothing like this had ever been done.

title: Seinfeld
synopsis: Jerry Seinfeld and Larry David's Seinfeld defined American comedy for a decade through its four magnificently neurotic New York protagonists and its refusal to allow them growth, redemption, or consequence — AFI's choice for the greatest comedy series ever made, its vocabulary entering the American language permanently.

title: Band of Brothers
synopsis: Steven Spielberg and Tom Hanks's Band of Brothers follows Easy Company from Normandy to Eagle's Nest through ten episodes of such sustained production ambition — $125 million, documentary-level fidelity to veterans' testimony — that it permanently raised the standard for historical drama on television.

title: Mad Men
synopsis: Matthew Weiner's Mad Men constructs the 1960s advertising world as a visual and moral argument that the decade's upheavals were experienced most acutely by those who had the most invested in the old order, Jon Hamm's Don Draper the most formally elegant antihero American television has produced.

title: Fleabag
synopsis: Phoebe Waller-Bridge's Fleabag deploys its nameless protagonist's direct address to the camera as a precision instrument of self-exposure, the comedy's formal intelligence matching its emotional courage — Andrew Scott's unnamed Priest and Waller-Bridge's Fleabag creating the finest love story in recent British television.

title: Chernobyl
synopsis: Johan Renck's Chernobyl dramatizes the 1986 nuclear disaster and its suppression with procedural fidelity so rigorous and Jared Harris's portrayal of Valery Legasov so completely inhabited that the series briefly held IMDB's highest-rated title — a distinction suggesting the audience understood it was watching something more like testimony than drama.

title: Succession
synopsis: Jesse Armstrong's Succession follows the Roy media dynasty's succession war through dialogue of Shakespearean wit and absolute moral bleakness, Jeremy Strong's Kendall and Brian Cox's Logan creating one of television's great central relationships and three Emmy wins for Outstanding Drama confirming the definitive series of the streaming era.

title: Planet Earth II
synopsis: David Attenborough's Planet Earth II presents the natural world through camera technology that had never previously captured it — from the snow leopard to the island iguana pursued by racer snakes — the series's visual splendor and Attenborough's narration together producing the most watched factual program in British television history.

title: The Honeymooners
synopsis: Jackie Gleason's Honeymooners establishes Ralph Kramden's bluster and frustration as the founding grammar of the American domestic sitcom, the chemistry between Gleason and Art Carney generating comedic partnership as instinctive and perfectly calibrated as any in the form.

title: All in the Family
synopsis: Norman Lear's All in the Family deploys Archie Bunker's unreconstructed prejudices as a laboratory for examining American social change, Carroll O'Connor's performance of magnificent comic bigotry so complex that conservatives claimed him as a hero while liberals laughed at him — the show's five consecutive Emmy wins confirming television could be simultaneously popular entertainment and moral argument.

title: MASH
synopsis: Larry Gelbart's MASH uses the Korean War as a container for Vietnam-era disillusionment, Alan Alda's Hawkeye Pierce embodying the argument that sanity in institutional madness requires a continuous performance of comic defiance — the eleven-year run and its record-breaking finale making it the most culturally significant comedy in American television history.

title: The X-Files
synopsis: Chris Carter's X-Files pairs Mulder's paranoid faith in extraterrestrial conspiracy with Scully's scientific skepticism in a mythology so carefully constructed that it generated a decade of devoted investigation, David Duchovny and Gillian Anderson's dynamic the finest intellectual partnership in television drama.

title: The West Wing
synopsis: Aaron Sorkin's West Wing creates an alternate America in which the presidency is conducted by principled intellectuals who speak in perfectly constructed paragraphs, Martin Sheen's Bartlet the most beloved fictional president in television history and the show's argument — that democratic governance is possible if people of good faith pursue it — more aspirational than descriptive but more necessary for that.

title: The Office (US)
synopsis: Greg Daniels's The Office adapts the Ricky Gervais original through Steve Carell's Michael Scott — a man whose desperate need for approval transforms every workplace interaction into performance — the American version finding in its ensemble cast something the British original never quite reached: a genuine portrait of how institutional life becomes family.

title: Game of Thrones
synopsis: David Benioff and D.B. Weiss's Game of Thrones adapted George R.R. Martin's fantasy epic across eight seasons that redefined the television spectacle, Peter Dinklage's Tyrion the finest performance in fantasy television and the show's record 59 Emmy Awards confirming a phenomenon that exceeded the form that contained it.

title: True Detective (Season 1)
synopsis: Nic Pizzolatto's True Detective Season 1 sends Matthew McConaughey's nihilist philosopher-detective and Woody Harrelson's conventional Louisiana lawman through a serial murder investigation across seventeen years, McConaughey's Rust Cohle — delivering Ligotti and Cioran through a bayou accent — producing the most philosophically ambitious performance in American crime television.

title: Atlanta
synopsis: Donald Glover's Atlanta follows Paper Boi's rap career and his cousin Earn's management attempts through a city the show treats as a surrealist canvas, its formal audacity — each episode a different genre experiment — and the specificity of its portrait of Black Southern life earning two Emmy Awards and establishing Glover as the most inventive auteur in American television.

title: Watchmen
synopsis: Damon Lindelof's Watchmen sequel series sends Regina King's Angela Abar through a Tulsa where the 1921 race massacre's trauma has never healed, the show's formal intelligence and Jean Smart's luminous Laurie Blake earning eleven Emmy Awards for the finest superhero television ever made.

title: The Last of Us
synopsis: Craig Mazin and Neil Druckmann's The Last of Us follows Joel and Ellie across a post-pandemic America where the emotional stakes of their relationship — surrogate father and daughter navigating a world that wants them dead — proved more devastating than any action sequence, earning the show the most watched premiere in HBO history.

title: Shōgun (2024)
synopsis: Rachel Kondo and Caillin Puente's Shogun reimagines James Clavell's feudal Japan epic through Hiroyuki Sanada's Lord Toranaga — a performance of inscrutable strategic intelligence — and Anna Sawai's Lady Mariko, the series's reverence for its Japanese cast and setting earning it a record Emmy sweep and the most acclaimed American prestige series of 2024.

title: The Manchurian Candidate
synopsis: John Frankenheimer's Manchurian Candidate transforms Cold War paranoia into a psychodrama of brainwashing and assassination, Frank Sinatra and Laurence Harvey's performances and the film's formal audacity producing a political thriller so prophetically accurate it was withdrawn from release after JFK's assassination.

title: Apocalypse Now
synopsis: Francis Ford Coppola's Apocalypse Now sends Martin Sheen's Captain Willard up the Mekong toward Marlon Brando's Colonel Kurtz through four years of catastrophic production and some of the most overwhelming cinema ever conceived, the Valkyries attack sequence and the film's refusal of moral resolution earning the Palme d'Or and two Academy Awards.

title: Fargo
synopsis: Joel and Ethan Coen's Fargo sends Frances McDormand's pregnant Minnesota police chief into a kidnapping scheme of spectacular incompetence, earning McDormand the first of her three Academy Awards and the Coens the Best Screenplay for a film shot in winter light so cold it constitutes its own moral commentary.

title: No Country for Old Men
synopsis: The Coens' No Country for Old Men sends hunter Llewelyn Moss across the Texas desert with drug money and Javier Bardem's Anton Chigurh behind him — the bolt-gun and its philosophy of fate the most formally perfect villain in American crime cinema — the film's four Academy Awards and refusal of conventional resolution confirming it as the decade's finest American film.

title: There Will Be Blood
synopsis: Paul Thomas Anderson's There Will Be Blood follows Daniel Day-Lewis's Daniel Plainview from lone prospector to oil dynasty through a performance universally acknowledged as one of the greatest ever committed to film, the confrontation between greed and faith earning Day-Lewis the Academy Award and the film its reputation as the defining American work of the 2000s.

title: Drive
synopsis: Nicolas Winding Refn's Drive follows Ryan Gosling's Hollywood stuntman through a Cannes Best Director-winning exercise in stylized violence and silence, the film's influence — its neon aesthetics, its contrast of tenderness and brutality — disproportionate to its modest box office and producing one of the decade's most imitated genre works.

title: Arrival
synopsis: Denis Villeneuve's Arrival sends Amy Adams's linguist into first contact with heptapod aliens whose non-linear language, once acquired, restructures human experience of time — the film's final revelation that grief and joy can be simultaneous rather than sequential generating the most philosophically moving ending in modern science fiction.

title: The Irishman
synopsis: Martin Scorsese's Irishman conducts its three-and-a-half-hour inquiry into Frank Sheeran's mob life through De Niro, Pesci, and Pacino's performances of age and diminishment, the accumulation of regret producing the most elegiac work of Scorsese's career and a farewell to the gangster genre that invented him.

title: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
synopsis: Quentin Tarantino's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood inhabits 1969 Los Angeles through Leonardo DiCaprio's fading TV actor and Brad Pitt's stuntman-companion with such atmospheric and cinematic love that the film earns its revisionist conclusion — the Sharon Tate murders averted by the specific skills of the people who would have been its victims.

title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
synopsis: Celine Sciamma's Portrait of a Lady on Fire follows painter Marianne's clandestine sessions with the reluctant Heloise on an isolated Breton island, the film's visual argument — that to be seen is to be loved, that looking is already a form of intimacy — conducted through glances and firelight.

title: Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles
synopsis: Chantal Akerman's Jeanne Dielman presents three days of a Brussels widow's household routines in real time, the film's radical patience making domestic labor's invisible weight fully visible until the disruption in the third day's routine opens an abyss, making it the Sight and Sound poll's choice as the greatest film ever made.

title: Twin Peaks
synopsis: David Lynch and Mark Frost's Twin Peaks sent FBI Agent Dale Cooper into a Pacific Northwest town of arresting strangeness to investigate the murder of Laura Palmer, the show's invention of dream-logic television — its casual supernatural menace, its comedy coexisting with genuine horror — making it the most formally influential American drama in television history.

title: I, Claudius
synopsis: Jack Pulman's I, Claudius follows Derek Jacobi's stammering scholar-emperor through the murders, sexual politics, and imperial madness of Rome from Augustus to Nero, the BBC production's theatrical intensity and Sian Phillips's magnificent Livia making it the finest historical drama in British television history.

title: The Crown
