synopsis: Peter Morgan's The Crown traces Queen Elizabeth II's reign through three sets of actors whose collective achievement — Claire Foy, Olivia Colman, Imelda Staunton each winning major awards — gives the series an authority no single performer could sustain, the production's extraordinary ambition earning 21 Emmy Awards.

title: Arrested Development (Seasons 1-3)
synopsis: Mitchell Hurwitz's Arrested Development deploys its Bluth family's spectacular dysfunction through a layered architecture of callbacks, foreshadowing, and jokes visible only on repeat viewing — the densest comic construction in American television — three Emmy wins understating its influence on every subsequent smart comedy.

title: Miniseries: Roots
synopsis: Alex Haley and David L. Wolper's Roots traces the Kinte family from Kunta Kinte's African capture through seven generations of American slavery to freedom, the 1977 broadcast attracting the largest audience in television history and generating the most significant national conversation about slavery's legacy that American television has ever provoked.

title: Barry Lyndon
synopsis: Stanley Kubrick's Barry Lyndon recreates 18th-century Europe through candlelit cinematography so beautiful that the Academy Award for cinematography was effectively inevitable, Ryan O'Neal's Irish rogue rising and falling through aristocratic society in a film whose formal perfection constitutes an argument about the relationship between beauty and moral vacancy.

title: Bicycle Thieves
synopsis: Vittorio De Sica's Bicycle Thieves follows a Roman worker's desperate search through postwar Rome for the bicycle stolen on his first day of a job he cannot afford to lose, the film's neorealist refusal of consolation and Lamberto Maggiorani's non-professional performance producing a work the AFI named the greatest foreign film ever made.

title: Deadwood
synopsis: David Milch's Deadwood inhabits the 1876 South Dakota gold-rush camp through language of such Shakespearean profanity and moral complexity that Ian McShane's Al Swearengen became the defining antiheroical performance of the prestige television era.

title: Wild Strawberries
synopsis: Ingmar Bergman's Wild Strawberries sends aging professor Isak Borg on a road trip to receive an honorary degree through flashbacks and dreams that constitute an inventory of failures — of love, of connection, of empathy — Victor Sjostrom's performance of a man taking quiet moral stock at the end of his life among the greatest in Swedish cinema.

title: Breathless
synopsis: Jean-Luc Godard's Breathless sends Jean-Paul Belmondo's small-time French hood through Paris after impulsively shooting a policeman, the film's jump cuts and direct address violating cinema's grammar so deliberately and joyfully that it effectively began a new era — Jean Seberg's American ingenue its moral conscience, Belmondo's Michel its charming amorality.

title: The 400 Blows
synopsis: Francois Truffaut's 400 Blows follows twelve-year-old Antoine Doinel through misunderstanding at school, misunderstanding at home, and a juvenile detention facility toward a freeze-frame at the ocean that is simultaneously escape and trap — Jean-Pierre Leaud's performance so naturally observed that the film became the most important debut in the history of the cinema.

title: L'Avventura
synopsis: Michelangelo Antonioni's L'Avventura sends wealthy Romans searching for Anna after her disappearance on a Sicilian island, the search gradually abandoned as her boyfriend and best friend begin an affair — the film's refusal of resolution and its portrait of emotional vacancy in the modern world creating a new cinematic language of alienation.

title: Scenes from a Marriage
synopsis: Ingmar Bergman's Scenes from a Marriage dismantles Johan and Marianne's marriage across six episodes of such intimate psychological precision — arguments, confessions, silences — that Swedish divorce rates reportedly rose after its broadcast, Liv Ullmann and Erland Josephson creating one of the most honest portraits of how love and resentment are inextricably entangled.

title: Cries and Whispers
synopsis: Ingmar Bergman's Cries and Whispers follows the dying Agnes and her two sisters through a country estate in deep winter, the film's red interiors and the performances of Harriet Andersson, Ingrid Thulin, and Liv Ullmann making it Bergman's most viscerally painful examination of the distance that exists even between those who love each other.

title: The Conformist
synopsis: Bernardo Bertolucci's Conformist sends a psychologically damaged fascist agent to Paris to assassinate his former professor, the film's examination of how political conformism is rooted in personal shame and Vittorio Storaro's cinematography — among the most beautiful ever shot — making it the finest Italian political film of its era.

title: Amarcord
synopsis: Federico Fellini's Amarcord recreates the Fascist-era Rimini of his childhood through seasonal vignettes that balance nostalgia and horror with exquisite precision, the film's episodic structure — a provincial town's collective memory — earning the Academy Award for Best Foreign Film and standing as Fellini's most humane work.

title: Cinema Paradiso
synopsis: Giuseppe Tornatore's Cinema Paradiso follows film director Salvatore's return to his Sicilian village for the funeral of Alfredo, the projectionist who was his first teacher, the film's warm nostalgia for the communal experience of cinema and the final reel of banned kisses assembling a portrait of how art shapes a life.

title: In the Mood for Love
synopsis: Wong Kar-wai's In the Mood for Love follows two neighbors who discover their spouses are having an affair and find themselves drawn together through the very restraint with which they resist their mutual feeling, Maggie Cheung and Tony Leung's performances conducted entirely in glances producing the most beautiful film about unexpressed desire in the history of cinema.

title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
synopsis: Michel Gondry's Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind follows Joel Barish's attempt to erase Clementine from his memory through a non-linear structure that makes forgetting feel like mourning, Jim Carrey and Kate Winslet's performances of love's specific textures earning Charlie Kaufman the Academy Award.

title: The Diving Bell and the Butterfly
synopsis: Julian Schnabel's Diving Bell and the Butterfly follows Elle editor Jean-Dominique Bauby's composition of his memoir through left-eye blinks after a brainstem stroke, the film's formal invention — the locked-off camera embodying locked-in syndrome — producing a work of such fierce beauty about consciousness and language that Schnabel won the Cannes Best Director prize.

title: 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days
synopsis: Cristian Mungiu's 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days follows two Romanian college students navigating an illegal abortion under Ceausescu's prohibition through a procedural realism so unsparing — the hotel room sequence conducted in a single shot that runs past endurance — that the Palme d'Or felt like recognition of something more than filmmaking.

title: Son of Saul
synopsis: Laszlo Nemes's Son of Saul follows a Hungarian Jewish Sonderkommando worker through Auschwitz-Birkenau over two days as he attempts to arrange a proper burial for a boy he believes is his son, the film's shallow depth of field keeping the camp's horror at the periphery of a face that must remain impassive.

title: Moonrise Kingdom
synopsis: Wes Anderson's Moonrise Kingdom sends two twelve-year-olds into a self-invented wilderness exile on a New England island in 1965, the film's precisely controlled visual grammar of nostalgia producing Anderson's most emotionally unguarded work and a portrait of childhood's seriousness that adults reliably underestimate.

title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
synopsis: Wes Anderson's Grand Budapest Hotel traces the adventures of legendary concierge Gustave H. and his lobby boy Zero across a European war through such exquisite visual invention and Ralph Fiennes's comic authority that the film became Anderson's most commercially successful and critically beloved work.

title: Lost in Translation
synopsis: Sofia Coppola's Lost in Translation strands a fading movie star and a neglected young wife in a Tokyo hotel's fluorescent limbo, Bill Murray and Scarlett Johansson's connection conducted in the language of shared insomnia and midnight karaoke constituting the finest portrait of elective loneliness in contemporary American cinema.

title: The Hurt Locker
synopsis: Kathryn Bigelow's Hurt Locker follows bomb disposal specialist William James through the adrenaline addiction of Baghdad urban warfare, Jeremy Renner's performance of a man who can only feel alive under maximum pressure earning Bigelow the first Best Director Oscar awarded to a woman.

title: The Truman Show
synopsis: Peter Weir's Truman Show sends Jim Carrey's Truman Burbank through the dawning recognition that his entire life is a television production, the film's comic surface concealing an inquiry into authenticity, surveillance, and the nature of consent that grew more accurate as reality television expanded to fill the culture.

title: Requiem for a Dream
synopsis: Darren Aronofsky's Requiem for a Dream follows four people through their various addictions with a formal intensity that transforms the destruction of aspiration into something approaching the operatic, Ellen Burstyn's performance of a woman eating herself alive with diet pills and loneliness earning her the New York Film Critics Best Actress award.

title: Hereditary
synopsis: Ari Aster's Hereditary follows the Graham family's disintegration after the death of a matriarch who kept secrets that her inheritance makes inescapable, Toni Collette's performance of grief collapsing into terror and the film's construction of dread establishing Aster as the most formally accomplished horror filmmaker of his generation.

title: Promising Young Woman
synopsis: Emerald Fennell's Promising Young Woman follows Cassie Thomas's controlled, methodical campaign of vengeance against the culture of complicity that destroyed her best friend, Carey Mulligan's performance of suppressed fury beneath perfect composure earning the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay.

title: The Shape of Water
synopsis: Guillermo del Toro's Shape of Water follows mute cleaning woman Elisa's love for an amphibious creature held captive in a Cold War government facility, Sally Hawkins's performance conducting its entire emotional range through physical expression and sign language in a film whose fairy-tale logic earned del Toro the Academy Award and Best Picture.

title: Marriage Story
synopsis: Noah Baumbach's Marriage Story follows a stage director and his actress wife through a coast-to-coast divorce with such emotional precision — Adam Driver and Scarlett Johansson's kitchen argument the finest scene of marital dissolution in American cinema — that Laura Dern's Academy Award-winning lawyer felt simultaneously comic and devastating.

title: The Pianist
synopsis: Roman Polanski's Pianist follows Polish-Jewish musician Wladyslaw Szpilman through the Warsaw Ghetto's destruction and six years of hiding with a formal restraint that refuses Holocaust sentimentality, Adrien Brody's emaciated performance earning the Academy Award and the film the Palme d'Or.

title: Belfast
synopsis: Kenneth Branagh's Belfast sends young Buddy through 1969 Northern Ireland's eruption of sectarian violence with documentary warmth — Judi Dench and Ciaran Hinds as grandparents, Jamie Dornan as a father refusing to stay and refusing to go — the black-and-white photography giving the memory its proper distance from the emotions it contains.

title: Drive My Car
synopsis: Ryusuke Hamaguchi's Drive My Car sends theater director Yusuke Kafuku through a three-hour meditation on grief, marriage, and performance, Hidetoshi Nishijima's formally reserved performance and the Chekhov adaptations generating a film of such unhurried emotional accumulation that its Academy Award for Best International Film felt overdue.

title: The Banshees of Inisherin
synopsis: Martin McDonagh's Banshees of Inisherin follows Padraic's incomprehension at Colm's decision to end their friendship on a small Irish island, Brendan Gleeson's terrible purpose and Colin Farrell's bewildered hurt generating a fable about creativity and the violence of withdrawal that earned eight Academy Award nominations.

title: Past Lives
synopsis: Celine Song's Past Lives follows Nora and Hae Sung's childhood connection in Seoul, separation, and reunion in New York twenty-four years later, Greta Lee's and Teo Yoo's performances finding the full weight of a road not taken in glances across a restaurant table — the film's final shot the most quietly devastating conclusion of its year.

title: American Fiction
synopsis: Cord Jefferson's American Fiction follows Monk Ellison's ironically intended street novel becoming a publishing phenomenon, Jeffrey Wright's performance of a man whose contempt for what the culture demands from Black writers is tested by his own exploitation of those demands earning the Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay.

title: Io Capitano
synopsis: Matteo Garrone's Io Capitano follows two Senegalese teenagers across the Sahara and the Mediterranean to Europe in a film of such documentary fidelity to the migrant experience that it earned Garrone the Silver Lion and stands as the most honest portrait of the 21st century's defining human crisis.

title: Touki Bouki
synopsis: Mambéty's exuberant Dakar fable follows a cattle-herder and a student dreaming of escape to Paris, scheming and stealing toward a ship that will not — or will not for both of them — leave the harbor, a jump-cut, time-folding burst of Senegalese New Wave that put African cinema on the international art-film map.

title: A Real Pain
synopsis: Jesse Eisenberg's A Real Pain sends two Jewish American cousins on a Holocaust memorial tour of Poland, Kieran Culkin's brilliant, self-destructive Benji and Eisenberg's anxious David navigating grief, family, and the impossibility of adequate response to historical atrocity — earning Culkin the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor.

title: I'm Still Here
synopsis: Walter Salles's I'm Still Here follows Eunice Paiva's thirty-year quest to establish the truth of her husband's disappearance under Brazil's military dictatorship, Fernanda Torres's performance earning the first Academy Award Best Actress nomination for a Brazilian actor and the film its Cannes Best Screenplay prize.

title: The Brutalist
synopsis: Brady Corbet's Brutalist sends Adrien Brody's Hungarian-Jewish architect to postwar America where his modernist genius finds patronage, exploitation, and eventual erasure, the film's three-and-a-half-hour scope and Brody's Academy Award-winning performance constituting the most ambitious American film of its decade.

title: Nickel Boys
synopsis: RaMell Ross's Nickel Boys adapts Colson Whitehead's novel through a subjective first-person cinematographic approach that makes the horror of Jim Crow reform school violence as immediate as the tenderness between Elwood and Turner, earning the New York Film Critics Best Film award.

title: September 5
synopsis: Tim Fehlbaum's September 5 follows the ABC Sports broadcast team's real-time decision to cover the 1972 Munich Olympics massacre live, the film's procedural tension about what to show and what to withhold producing the most formally intelligent film about media and catastrophe since Network.

title: Flow
synopsis: Gints Zilbalodis's Flow follows a cat through a flooded world populated only by animals — capybara, lemur, secretary bird — the animated film's wordless narrative and visual beauty earning the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and confirming the Latvian director as the most original animation voice since Miyazaki.

title: Goodfellas
synopsis: Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas traces Henry Hill's rise through the Lucchese crime family with a kinetic energy — the Copacabana tracking shot, the Layla montage, Ray Liotta's direct address — that makes the glamour of organized crime feel as immediate and irresistible as its narrator does, establishing the definitive template for the modern gangster film.

title: Fight Club
synopsis: David Fincher's Fight Club sends Edward Norton's insomniac office worker into Brad Pitt's Tyler Durden's anti-consumer underground, the film's sustained formal intensity and its central revelation generating a work whose cultural influence has far outlasted the controversy that greeted its release.

title: All Quiet on the Western Front
synopsis: Edward Berger's All Quiet on the Western Front returns to Remarque's WWI novel with a formal severity that refuses heroism at every turn, Felix Kammerer's performance of a young soldier watching his idealism dissolve in mud earning four Academy Awards and the film's devastating final minutes confirming the antiwar film's enduring necessity.

title: Joker
synopsis: Todd Phillips's Joker follows Arthur Fleck's socioeconomic descent into the clown-masked vigilante through Joaquin Phoenix's performance of compulsive physical transformation — the weight loss, the laugh, the dance — earning Phoenix the Academy Award and the film the Venice Golden Lion in the most divisive prestige superhero film ever made.

title: The Holdovers
synopsis: Alexander Payne's Holdovers strands curmudgeonly classics teacher Paul Hunham and grieving student Angus Tully at a Massachusetts prep school over Christmas break, Paul Giamatti's performance of magnificent misanthropic warmth and Da'Vine Joy Randolph's Academy Award-winning Mary Lamb making it the finest American comedy-drama of its year.

title: Aftersun
synopsis: Charlotte Wells's Aftersun follows a young woman's revisitation of footage from a Scottish holiday taken with her father when she was eleven, Paul Mescal's contained performance and the film's formal beauty — the Super 8, the final disco sequence — making it the most formally devastating debut of its decade.

title: All of Us Strangers
synopsis: Andrew Haigh's All of Us Strangers sends screenwriter Adam into a relationship with his neighbor Paul while also, impossibly, revisiting his childhood home to find his parents still alive in 1987, Andrew Scott's and Paul Mescal's performances and the film's refusal to distinguish between grief and love generating the most emotionally overwhelming film of 2023.

title: Some Like It Hot
synopsis: Billy Wilder's Some Like It Hot sends Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon's jazz musicians in drag through a 1929 Miami resort after witnessing the Saint Valentine's Day Massacre, Marilyn Monroe's Sugar Kane — blissfully unaware of everyone's deceptions — producing the AFI's choice for the greatest comedy film ever made.

title: The Third Man
synopsis: Carol Reed's Third Man sends Holly Martins through postwar Vienna's sewers and moral ambiguity to discover that his old friend Harry Lime — Orson Welles's magnificent ten minutes of screen time — is responsible for deaths Martins must reckon with, Anton Karas's zither score creating the most distinctive sound in postwar cinema and the Sight and Sound poll confirming it as the greatest British film ever made.

title: Tokyo Story
synopsis: Yasujiro Ozu's Tokyo Story sends elderly parents to visit their adult children in Tokyo and finds them politely, devastatingly unwelcome, the film's formal patience and rejection of dramatic incident in favor of the accumulation of small neglects producing what Roger Ebert called one of the few films he would describe as perfect.

title: The Wages of Fear
synopsis: Clouzot's existentialist suspense classic strands four desperate Europeans in a Latin-American oil-company town, then hires them to drive two truckloads of unstable nitroglycerin across two hundred miles of mountain road — a film whose extended set-pieces (the gravel ridge, the oil pool) are studied as the apex of pure-mechanics suspense filmmaking.

title: Dr. Zhivago
synopsis: David Lean's Dr. Zhivago follows Russian physician-poet Yuri's divided loves across the upheaval of revolution and civil war, Maurice Jarre's Lara's Theme and Robert Bolt's screenplay combining with the film's extraordinary scope to make it one of the great sweeping romantic epics and the highest-grossing film of 1965.

title: Rosemary's Baby
synopsis: Roman Polanski's Rosemary's Baby follows a young wife's mounting paranoia that her neighbors and husband have conspired to use her body for a Satanic ritual, Mia Farrow's performance of vulnerability curdling into isolation as the film dismantles the safety of domestic life with surgical precision.

title: All the President's Men
synopsis: Alan J. Pakula's All the President's Men follows Washington Post reporters Woodward and Bernstein's dogged unraveling of the Watergate scandal, the film's procedural intelligence and Redford and Hoffman's precisely matched chemistry producing the most gripping political journalism film in the history of American cinema.

title: The Simpsons
synopsis: Lucille Ball's Simpsons — no, Matt Groening's The Simpsons defined American satirical comedy for a generation through its four magnificently specific Springfield family and the town around them, AFI's choice for the greatest comedy series ever made, its vocabulary entering the American language permanently.

title: Frasier
dir: David Angell, Peter Casey, David Lee
synopsis: The Frasier show follows pompous Seattle radio psychiatrist Frasier Crane — Kelsey Grammer's magnificent performance sustained across 11 seasons — and his equally refined but neurotic family and colleagues in a comedy of such sustained verbal elegance that its 37 Emmy Awards and 5 consecutive Best Comedy wins remain unsurpassed.

title: The General
synopsis: Buster Keaton's The General transforms a Civil War train-theft into the most breathtaking physical comedy ever filmed — a stone-faced engineer pursuing his stolen locomotive with a precision of gag construction so mathematically perfect that every subsequent action comedy exists in its gravitational field.

title: Metropolis
synopsis: Fritz Lang's expressionist vision of a stratified future city invented the visual vocabulary of science fiction cinema and remains the genre's most prophetic and architecturally stunning achievement.

title: Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans
synopsis: Murnau's luminous film follows a farmer tempted to murder his wife, then redeemed through rediscovered love — the camera's revolutionary fluid movement winning the first-ever Academy Award.

title: The Jazz Singer
synopsis: The first feature with synchronized dialogue shattered cinema history with Al Jolson's "Wait a minute, you ain't heard nothin' yet!" — a technological earthquake that rebuilt an industry.

title: The Passion of Joan of Arc
synopsis: Dreyer's transcendent masterpiece reduces Joan's trial to extreme close-ups — Falconetti's face becoming a landscape of suffering widely regarded as the greatest single performance in cinema history.

title: City Lights
synopsis: Chaplin's City Lights follows the Tramp's devotion to a blind flower girl, its final scene — when she sees him for the first time — representing what James Agee called the finest moment in cinema history.

title: M
synopsis: Lang's M casts Peter Lorre as a child murderer hunted by police and criminals alike, inventing the serial killer genre and establishing suspense as cinema's most morally complex mode.

title: Frankenstein
synopsis: James Whale's Frankenstein transforms Shelley's novel into the primal horror myth of the twentieth century — Boris Karloff's Monster establishing the template for every creature feature that followed.

title: Grand Hotel
synopsis: Grand Hotel gathers Garbo, Crawford, and the Barrymores into a Berlin luxury hotel for an ensemble drama that established the template for every multi-character narrative that followed.

title: King Kong
dir: Merian C. Cooper, Ernest B. Schoedsack
synopsis: King Kong remains cinema's most potent beauty-and-beast myth — the ape's final stand atop the Empire State Building so mythically resonant it transcends its stop-motion origins to define American cinema.

title: It Happened One Night
synopsis: Capra's screwball masterpiece — a runaway heiress and wisecracking reporter on a cross-country bus — created the romantic comedy and was the first film to sweep all five major Academy Awards.

title: The 39 Steps
synopsis: Hitchcock's The 39 Steps perfected the wrong-man thriller — an innocent man pursued across Scotland by police and spies — establishing the template he would refine for four more decades.

title: Modern Times
synopsis: Chaplin's final bow as the Tramp sends his beloved character through industrial capitalism's machinery — the assembly-line gag among cinema's most famous — creating the definitive satire of mechanized modernity.

title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
synopsis: Disney's colossal gamble created the first full-length animated feature in cinema history, proving so commercially overwhelming it became the highest-grossing sound film to that date.

title: The Rules of the Game
synopsis: Renoir's devastating satire of class entanglements during a country-house weekend — hated by audiences, censored, lost in WWII — was painstakingly reconstructed and recognized as one of the supreme achievements of cinema.

title: Gone with the Wind
synopsis: Fleming's sweeping Civil War epic follows Scarlett O'Hara's survival through the destruction of the antebellum South — 10 Academy Awards, the most commercially successful film ever made adjusted for inflation.

title: The Wizard of Oz
synopsis: Fleming's fairy tale transformed Baum's story into America's foundational cinematic myth — the transition from sepia to Technicolor among cinema's most magical moments, "Over the Rainbow" the most beloved film song ever.

title: Mr. Smith Goes to Washington
synopsis: Capra's idealistic senator discovers corruption, and Jimmy Stewart's filibuster became the definitive screen portrayal of democratic idealism.

title: Stagecoach
synopsis: Ford's Stagecoach invented the modern Western by sending mismatched travelers across Apache territory, establishing both Ford's visual grandeur and John Wayne's iconic persona.

title: Ninotchka
synopsis: Lubitsch's Ninotchka deploys Greta Garbo as a stern Soviet envoy melted by Paris and charm — "Garbo Laughs!" — the Lubitsch Touch at its most effervescent.

title: The Grapes of Wrath
synopsis: Ford's Dust Bowl epic follows the Joad family's migration west, Henry Fonda's Tom Joad becoming the enduring symbol of working-class resilience in American cinema.

title: The Great Dictator
synopsis: Chaplin's audacious Hitler satire climaxes in a direct-to-camera plea for humanity that remains the most emotionally powerful political speech in film history.

title: Fantasia
synopsis: Disney merged classical music with experimental animation — audiences were baffled, but generations recognized it as the most ambitious artistic experiment in commercial animation history.

title: The Maltese Falcon
synopsis: Huston's debut crystallized film noir — Bogart's Sam Spade navigating duplicitous fortune-seekers pursuing a jeweled falcon, deception itself the film's true subject.

title: Bambi
synopsis: Disney's Bambi reduces the forest to emotional essentials — birth, first love, and the death of a mother so devastating it permanently traumatized millions of children.

title: Mrs. Miniver
synopsis: Wyler's wartime drama follows an English family enduring the Blitz — Churchill said it was worth more than a fleet of destroyers for Allied morale.

title: Pinocchio
synopsis: Disney's Pinocchio achieved a level of animated realism and emotional complexity that many consider the pinnacle of hand-drawn animation — "When You Wish Upon a Star" became the Disney anthem.

title: The African Queen
synopsis: Huston pairs a gin-soaked riverboat captain with a prim missionary on an African river — Bogart and Hepburn's combative chemistry producing one of cinema's most enduring romantic pairings.

title: Shane
synopsis: Stevens distills the Western to its mythic essence — a mysterious gunfighter defends homesteaders then rides away wounded, the boy's cry of "Shane! Come back!" echoing across decades.

title: The Night of the Hunter
synopsis: Laughton's only film — a catastrophe that ended his directing career — follows children fleeing a preacher with LOVE and HATE tattooed on his knuckles, its expressionist imagery unlike anything in American cinema.

title: Rebel Without a Cause
synopsis: Ray's landmark teen drama channels postwar alienation through James Dean's inarticulate anguish — Dean's death before release sealing his image as eternal youth.

title: The Seventh Seal
synopsis: Bergman's medieval knight playing chess with Death — its central image so universally recognizable that even those who've never seen the film know its iconography.

title: Paths of Glory
synopsis: Kubrick's devastating film follows a colonel defending soldiers scapegoated for a suicidal WWI assault — banned in France for depicting French military injustice.

title: Touch of Evil
synopsis: Welles opens with cinema's most celebrated tracking shot — three minutes following a car bomb — then plunges into a corrupt borderlands thriller restored to his vision in 1998.

title: Breakfast at Tiffany's
synopsis: Edwards transforms Capote's novella into a Manhattan fairy tale — Hepburn's Holly Golightly singing "Moon River" on a fire escape becoming the most iconic image of cosmopolitan femininity.

title: The Great Escape
synopsis: Sturges transforms a true POW mass-breakout into the quintessential adventure film — McQueen's motorcycle chase, Bernstein's march theme, and three hours of pure exhilaration.

title: In the Heat of the Night
synopsis: Jewison sends Poitier's detective into hostile Mississippi — his confrontation with Steiger's bigoted sheriff producing cinema's most powerful portrayal of racial tension and grudging respect.

title: The Sting
synopsis: Hill reunites Newman and Redford for an elaborately constructed Depression-era con game whose twist-upon-twist plot mechanics became the template for every heist film that followed.

title: The Conversation
synopsis: Coppola's paranoid masterpiece follows a surveillance expert who overhears what may be a murder plot, the film's claustrophobic moral architecture anticipating Watergate with uncanny precision.

title: Dog Day Afternoon
synopsis: Lumet's true-crime masterpiece follows a botched Brooklyn bank robbery that becomes a media circus, Pacino's "Attica!" chant galvanizing both hostages and crowd into a portrait of American desperation.

title: Nashville
synopsis: Altman weaves 24 characters through five days in Nashville into an American panorama whose overlapping dialogue, improvisational performances, and mosaic structure redefined what ensemble cinema could achieve.

title: Alien
synopsis: Ridley Scott's Alien fuses science fiction with horror aboard a grimy commercial spaceship where something lethal is gestating — Sigourney Weaver's Ripley redefining the action heroine and H.R. Giger's creature design becoming the most iconic monster since Karloff's Frankenstein.

title: Superman
synopsis: Donner's Superman proved superhero films could be both spectacular and sincere — Christopher Reeve's dual performance as Clark Kent and Superman so definitive that no subsequent portrayal has escaped its gravitational pull.

title: The Shining
synopsis: Kubrick transforms King's haunted-hotel novel into an architecturally precise nightmare — Nicholson's Jack Torrance descending into axe-wielding madness through the Overlook's infinite corridors, the film's cold geometry generating dread no warm-blooded horror film has matched.

title: Gandhi
synopsis: Attenborough's sprawling biography follows Mohandas Gandhi from South African lawyer to spiritual leader of Indian independence — Ben Kingsley's transformative performance earning the film eight Academy Awards.

title: The Breakfast Club
synopsis: Hughes locks five high-school archetypes in Saturday detention and lets them dismantle their social armor, the result becoming the definitive teen film — a generation's shorthand for the discovery that identity is more complex than any label allows.

title: Aliens
synopsis: Cameron transforms Scott's claustrophobic horror into an adrenaline-fueled war film — Ripley's transformation from survivor to warrior mother creating the template for the modern action heroine.

title: Stand by Me
synopsis: Reiner's Stephen King adaptation follows four boys on a Labor Day hike to find a dead body — a journey that doubles as the last innocent adventure before adulthood claims them, its emotional truth making it the definitive coming-of-age film.

title: The Princess Bride
synopsis: Reiner's fairy-tale deconstruction — simultaneously a sincere romance, sharp parody, and quotable adventure — became the most beloved cult film of the 1980s, its dialogue entering the common vocabulary of an entire generation.

title: Do the Right Thing
synopsis: Spike Lee's incendiary Brooklyn heatwave drama follows a single block's escalating racial tensions to an explosive climax, the film's refusal to provide moral resolution forcing audiences to confront their own complicity.

title: The Matrix
synopsis: The Wachowskis' The Matrix fused cyberpunk philosophy with Hong Kong martial arts into a reality-bending blockbuster whose "bullet time" sequences and red-pill/blue-pill iconography permanently altered both action cinema and popular culture.

title: Se7en
synopsis: Fincher's rain-soaked serial-killer thriller follows two detectives pursuing a murderer using the seven deadly sins as a framework, its nightmarish final act delivering one of cinema's most devastating twists.

title: Heat
synopsis: Mann's epic crime saga pits Pacino's obsessed detective against De Niro's disciplined thief — their first-ever shared scene in a diner becoming one of cinema's most legendary actor confrontations.

title: Good Will Hunting
synopsis: Van Sant's drama of a janitor genius grappling with emotional armor features Robin Williams's finest dramatic performance — his "It's not your fault" breakthrough the emotional core of a film that launched Damon and Affleck from unknowns to superstars.

title: Life Is Beautiful
synopsis: Benigni's audacious Holocaust fable follows a father who shields his son from concentration camp horror by pretending it's an elaborate game — polarizing critics but winning three Academy Awards and massive worldwide audiences.

title: The Big Lebowski
synopsis: The Coens' L.A. noir-as-stoner-comedy follows The Dude through a labyrinthine kidnapping plot he's too laid-back to navigate, the film's quotability and Bridges's iconic performance spawning a genuine religion (Dudeism) and the biggest cult following since Rocky Horror.

title: The Sixth Sense
synopsis: Shyamalan's ghost story follows a child psychologist treating a boy who sees dead people, its final revelation recontextualizing every preceding scene and becoming the most famous twist ending in modern cinema.

title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon
synopsis: Ang Lee's wuxia epic fused martial arts spectacle with literary romance — its rooftop chase and bamboo forest duel achieving a balletic beauty that brought Chinese cinema to global mainstream audiences.

title: Amélie
synopsis: Jeunet's whimsical Parisian fairy tale follows a shy waitress orchestrating anonymous acts of kindness, its candy-colored visual style and Audrey Tautou's luminous performance creating the most joyful European film of the 21st century.

title: The Incredibles
synopsis: Bird's superhero family comedy combines Pixar's emotional intelligence with genuine action-film thrills — a family of retired superheroes rediscovering their powers doubles as a meditation on mediocrity versus excellence.

title: Pan's Labyrinth
synopsis: Del Toro's dark fairy tale interweaves a girl's mythic quest through an underground labyrinth with the brutal reality of Franco's Spain, the fantasy and horror mirroring each other in a film that proves fairy tales were always about surviving real monsters.

title: Ratatouille
synopsis: Bird's Parisian cooking fable follows a rat pursuing haute cuisine dreams despite nature's cruelest joke — being a rat — its climactic scene where a food critic is transported to childhood by a simple dish achieving the most emotionally devastating moment in Pixar's history.

title: Black Swan
synopsis: Aronofsky's psychological thriller follows a ballerina's descent into madness as she prepares for Swan Lake, Portman's ferocious performance blurring reality and hallucination into dance cinema's most visceral nightmare.

title: Django Unchained
synopsis: Tarantino's revisionist Western follows a freed slave and a German bounty hunter across the antebellum South in a blood-soaked liberation fantasy that weaponizes genre entertainment against American slavery.

title: Inside Out
synopsis: Docter's brilliant conceit personifies a girl's emotions as characters inside her mind — Joy and Sadness's journey revealing that sadness is not joy's enemy but its essential partner, a truth so profoundly expressed that adults weep more than children.

title: Spotlight
synopsis: McCarthy's procedural thriller follows the Boston Globe's investigation of systemic child abuse in the Catholic Church, its restraint and journalistic rigor achieving a moral fury more devastating than any melodrama.

title: Manchester by the Sea
synopsis: Lonergan's devastating drama follows a handyman forced to confront the tragedy he's spent years fleeing when his brother dies and he's named guardian of his nephew — Casey Affleck's performance of suppressed grief among the most wrenching in modern cinema.

title: Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri
synopsis: McDonagh's dark comedy follows a mother who rents three billboards to shame the local police over her daughter's unsolved murder, Frances McDormand's ferocious performance driving a film about rage, grief, and the impossibility of redemption.

title: Coco
synopsis: Pixar's celebration of Día de los Muertos follows a boy into the Land of the Dead to discover his family's musical legacy — its climactic "Remember Me" scene achieving emotional devastation that transcends language and culture.

title: Roma
synopsis: Cuarón's luminous black-and-white memory film recreates his 1970s Mexico City childhood through the eyes of the indigenous domestic worker who raised him — personal filmmaking of such immersive beauty it redefined what a Netflix film could be.

title: A Star Is Born
synopsis: Cooper's directorial debut retells the classic Hollywood story of a fading rock star who discovers and falls in love with a young singer, Lady Gaga's raw performance and "Shallow" earning the film massive commercial and critical success.

Mendes's WWI drama follows two soldiers racing across no-man's-land to deliver a message that could save 1,600 lives, the "one continuous shot" illusion creating an unprecedented real-time immersion in wartime horror.

title: Knives Out
synopsis: Johnson's whodunit reinvention assembles an all-star ensemble around a dead mystery novelist's mansion, then systematically subverts every genre expectation into a gleeful commentary on class, immigration, and the detective story itself.

title: Minari
synopsis: Chung's semi-autobiographical drama follows a Korean-American family pursuing the American Dream on an Arkansas farm — Youn Yuh-jung's scene-stealing grandmother earning a historic Oscar.

title: Beau Travail
synopsis: Denis's nearly dialogue-free Djibouti reverie watches French Foreign Legion soldiers ironing shirts, digging trenches, and dancing in chiseled formations — until adjudant-chef Galoup (Denis Lavant) develops a wordless obsession with a new recruit that destroys his career, ending in the most quoted closing dance in modern cinema.

title: CODA
synopsis: Heder's crowd-pleasing drama follows the only hearing member of a deaf family torn between her singing ambitions and her family's dependence on her — Troy Kotsur's performance earning a historic Oscar as the first deaf male winner.

title: The Fabelmans
synopsis: Spielberg's autobiographical portrait of his filmmaking origins — a boy discovering cinema's power to reveal truth through his parents' troubled marriage — achieves the director's most emotionally naked work.

title: The Zone of Interest
synopsis: Glazer's chilling Holocaust film depicts the domestic bliss of the Auschwitz commandant's family in their garden next to the camp wall — the horror entirely off-screen, present only as distant sounds and smoke, creating the most formally radical Holocaust film ever made.

title: Anatomy of a Fall
synopsis: Triet's Cannes winner puts a marriage under forensic examination through a courtroom trial — did she push him? — Sandra Hüller's controlled fury producing the most riveting performance in a year of remarkable performances.

title: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse
dir: Joaquim Dos Santos, Kemp Powers, Justin K. Thompson
synopsis: The sequel to the groundbreaking Spider-Verse pushes animation further into uncharted territory — every scene a different visual style — while telling a multiverse story about destiny, choice, and what makes a hero.

title: Reservoir Dogs
synopsis: Tarantino's debut reassembled the heist film by showing only the before and after — never the robbery itself — launching the most influential American filmmaking career since Scorsese.

title: The English Patient
synopsis: Minghella's sumptuous adaptation of Ondaatje's novel interweaves a burned pilot's memories of a doomed Saharan love affair with his nurse's present-day healing — lush, literary filmmaking at its most ravishing.

title: Traffic
synopsis: Soderbergh's kaleidoscopic drug-war epic interweaves three storylines — a judge, a DEA agent, a trafficker's wife — across the US-Mexico border, its color-coded cinematography becoming a signature of early 2000s cinema.

title: A Beautiful Mind
synopsis: Howard's biography of mathematician John Nash follows his genius and schizophrenia with a structural trick that places the audience inside his delusions — Crowe's performance earning the film four Academy Awards.

title: Kill Bill: Volume 1
synopsis: Tarantino's revenge epic sends Uma Thurman's Bride on a blood-spattered quest through yakuza clans and desert trailers, its virtuosic blend of samurai cinema, spaghetti Western, and anime creating the most stylistically audacious action film of the decade.

title: Mystic River
synopsis: Eastwood's Greek tragedy set in working-class Boston follows three childhood friends reconnected by murder, Sean Penn's volcanic grief and Tim Robbins's haunted damage earning both Academy Awards.

title: La Dolce Vita
synopsis: Fellini's seven-night Roman odyssey follows Marcello Mastroianni's gossip-columnist Marcello as he drifts through aristocrats, intellectuals, miracles, and Anita Ekberg's Trevi Fountain wade — the film whose central character's photographer-friend Paparazzo gave the world its word for tabloid hounds and whose moral exhaustion redefined what a postwar European drama could look like.

title: The Father
synopsis: Zeller's debut places the audience inside the disorienting experience of dementia — the apartment keeps changing, characters shift identities — Anthony Hopkins's devastating performance earning him a record-setting Oscar at 83.

title: RRR
synopsis: Rajamouli's Telugu-language action epic fuses history, mythology, and Bollywood spectacle into three hours of unrestrained maximalist cinema — its "Naatu Naatu" dance number winning the Oscar and introducing global audiences to Indian commercial cinema's full power.

title: The Batman
synopsis: Reeves reimagines Batman as a noir detective story drenched in Gotham rain, Robert Pattinson's haunted Bruce Wayne proving that the character still has unexplored psychological territory after thirty years of screen iterations.

title: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
synopsis: The Pythons' micro-budget medieval farce — coconut horses, a killer rabbit, a shrubbery-demanding knight — demolished Arthurian legend with such quotable absurdity that it became the most beloved comedy of the 1970s.

title: Friends
synopsis: Crane and Kauffman's six-friends-in-Manhattan sitcom became the defining show of the 1990s, its ensemble chemistry so effortless that it generated a $1B+ syndication empire and remains the most streamed classic sitcom worldwide.

title: Star Trek: The Original Series
synopsis: Roddenberry's vision of a multiracial crew exploring the galaxy became television's most consequential cancelled show — its themes of diversity, diplomacy, and optimistic futurism spawning a franchise worth billions.

title: The Mary Tyler Moore Show
synopsis: Brooks and Burns created television's first single-working-woman comedy, Mary Richards's Minneapolis newsroom becoming a template for workplace ensemble that every subsequent sitcom follows.

title: Saturday Night Live
synopsis: Michaels's late-night institution has launched more comedy careers than any other show in history — from Belushi to Murphy to Fey to Mulaney — its live format making it America's premiere comedic testing ground for half a century.

title: Hill Street Blues
synopsis: Bochco and Kozoll's gritty police procedural invented the serialized ensemble drama — overlapping storylines, hand-held cameras, ambiguous morality — creating the template that every prestige drama from ER to The Wire would follow.

title: Cheers
dir: James Burrows, Glen Charles, Les Charles (creators)
synopsis: The Charles Brothers and Burrows created the perfect bar — a place where everybody knows your name — Ted Danson's Sam Malone and Shelley Long's Diane Chambers generating the greatest will-they/won't-they in sitcom history.

title: The Golden Girls
synopsis: Harris's Miami-set sitcom proved that four older women sharing a house could be sharper, funnier, and more sexually candid than any youth-targeted comedy — its progressive humor on aging, sexuality, and friendship still radical.

title: Law & Order
synopsis: Wolf's procedural split the hour between cops and lawyers with a "ripped from the headlines" formula so durable it spawned a franchise spanning over 1,500 episodes across multiple series.

title: ER
synopsis: Crichton's Chicago emergency room drama combined kinetic camerawork with emotionally devastating storytelling, its first five seasons achieving a creative peak that made it the most-watched drama on television.

title: Buffy the Vampire Slayer
synopsis: Whedon's genre-defying series used vampire mythology as metaphor for adolescent trauma, its feminist heroine, serialized storytelling, and tonal versatility proving that genre television could achieve literary ambition.

title: Sex and the City
synopsis: Star's Manhattan-set comedy followed four women navigating sex, friendship, and designer shoes with a candor that shattered television's treatment of female sexuality and spawned a franchise worth hundreds of millions.

title: Six Feet Under
synopsis: Ball's funeral-home family drama used death as a prism through which to examine life with unflinching intimacy — its series finale, set to Sia's "Breathe Me," universally regarded as the greatest ending in television history.

title: Curb Your Enthusiasm
synopsis: Larry David plays a fictionalized version of himself whose pathological honesty and social blindness generate escalating catastrophes — the definitive cringe comedy and the spiritual sequel to Seinfeld.

title: The Office (UK)
synopsis: Gervais and Merchant's mockumentary set in a Slough paper company — David Brent's delusional self-regard generating the most excruciating comedy ever broadcast — reinvented the sitcom and spawned adaptations in 10 countries.

title: Lost
dir: J.J. Abrams, Damon Lindelof, Jeffrey Lieber (creators)
synopsis: Abrams and Lindelof's island mystery became the most obsessively analyzed show of the internet age — its mythology-box structure, flashback innovation, and ensemble drama inspiring every subsequent puzzle-box series.

title: Battlestar Galactica
synopsis: Moore's reimagining transformed a campy 1970s space opera into the most politically sophisticated sci-fi series ever made — its post-9/11 allegory of survival, democracy, and occupation surpassing most prestige dramas in ambition.

title: 30 Rock
synopsis: Fey's backstage comedy about a fictional NBC variety show packs more jokes per minute than any other sitcom — its density rewarding rewatching and Alec Baldwin's Jack Donaghy becoming television's finest comic creation of the decade.

title: Friday Night Lights
synopsis: Berg's Texas high-school football drama transcended its sports premise to become television's most emotionally authentic portrait of small-town America — "Clear eyes, full hearts, can't lose" entering the American lexicon.

title: Parks and Recreation
synopsis: Daniels and Schur's Pawnee, Indiana comedy found its voice when it pivoted from cringe to warmth — Amy Poehler's Leslie Knope becoming TV's most optimistic protagonist and the show the rare sitcom that celebrates government service.

title: Downton Abbey
synopsis: Fellowes's Edwardian country-house saga followed the Crawley family and their servants through war, social upheaval, and romantic entanglements, becoming the biggest British TV export since Monty Python.

title: Veep
synopsis: Iannucci's political satire follows a vice president through the absurdities of American government — Julia Louis-Dreyfus's Selina Meyer, vain, foul-mouthed, and indomitable, earning an unprecedented six consecutive Emmy Awards.

title: Fargo (TV)
synopsis: Hawley's anthology series transplants the Coen Brothers' moral universe to new settings each season — Minnesota nice colliding with absolute evil — achieving the rare feat of honoring source material while surpassing it.

title: Better Call Saul
synopsis: Gilligan and Gould's prequel transforms Breaking Bad's comic lawyer into a tragic figure — Bob Odenkirk's Jimmy McGill evolving into Saul Goodman with such deliberate inevitability that many consider it superior to its predecessor.

title: The Americans
synopsis: Weisberg's Cold War thriller follows Soviet spies posing as a suburban American couple — the marriage itself the show's true subject — achieving the most devastating series finale since Six Feet Under.

title: Stranger Things
synopsis: The Duffer Brothers' 1980s-set supernatural thriller channels Spielberg, King, and Carpenter into a nostalgic adventure that became Netflix's biggest cultural phenomenon and a global pop-culture touchstone.

title: The Handmaid's Tale
synopsis: Miller's adaptation of Atwood's dystopian novel follows a woman enslaved as a reproductive vessel in a theocratic America — Elisabeth Moss's ferocious performance making it Hulu's signature show and the defining dystopian drama of the Trump era.

title: Big Little Lies
synopsis: Vallée's Monterey murder mystery assembled Kidman, Witherspoon, Woodley, Kravitz, and Dern into television's most formidable ensemble — Kidman's portrayal of domestic abuse earning acclaim as the finest dramatic performance on TV that year.

title: Barry
synopsis: Berg and Hader's dark comedy follows a hitman who discovers acting — then can't quit either profession — Hader's performance navigating tonal shifts from slapstick to horror with precision rivaling the best dramatic actors of his generation.

title: Euphoria
synopsis: Levinson's hyper-stylized teen drama explores addiction, identity, and trauma through kaleidoscopic visuals — Zendaya's raw performance as a recovering addict earning her a historic Emmy at age 24.

title: Ted Lasso
dir: Jason Sudeikis, Bill Lawrence, Brendan Hunt, Joe Kelly (creators)
synopsis: Sudeikis's American football coach managing an English soccer team became the pandemic's defining comfort show — its radical message that kindness and emotional intelligence are not weaknesses but superpowers.

title: The Queen's Gambit
synopsis: Frank's limited series follows an orphaned chess prodigy through addiction and Cold War tournaments — Anya Taylor-Joy's mesmerizing performance making chess cinematic and sparking a global chess boom.

title: Squid Game
synopsis: Hwang's Korean survival drama pits desperate debtors against each other in deadly children's games, its anti-capitalist allegory becoming the most-watched Netflix show in history and a global cultural phenomenon.

title: Severance
synopsis: Erickson's dystopian workplace thriller imagines employees whose memories are surgically split between work and personal selves — a Kafkaesque parable of corporate dehumanization wrapped in the decade's most addictive mystery.

title: The Bear
synopsis: Storer's high-pressure kitchen drama follows a fine-dining chef returning to run his dead brother's Chicago beef stand — its real-time cooking sequences generating anxiety levels that make it the most physically stressful show on television.

title: House of the Dragon
synopsis: Condal and Martin's Thrones prequel chronicles the Targaryen civil war with a character focus that recaptured what made the original series compelling — its depiction of female political power its most distinctive contribution.

title: The White Lotus
synopsis: White's luxury-resort satire dissects wealth, privilege, and entitlement through guests behaving badly in paradise — its razor-sharp class commentary and memorable performances making each season an event.

title: Only Murders in the Building
synopsis: Martin and Hoffman's cozy mystery follows three true-crime-podcast-obsessed neighbors investigating murders in their Upper West Side building — Martin and Short's chemistry proving that comedy legends only improve with age.

title: Abbott Elementary
synopsis: Brunson's mockumentary about a Philadelphia public school celebrates underfunded teachers with warmth and sharp humor, its grassroots success reviving the broadcast sitcom at a moment when everyone had written the format off.

title: Slow Horses
synopsis: Herron's adaptation follows disgraced MI5 agents banished to bureaucratic exile who keep stumbling into real espionage — Gary Oldman's magnificently disheveled Jackson Lamb making it the best spy series since the Smiley era.

title: Baby Reindeer
synopsis: Gadd's autobiographical limited series about being stalked by a woman he showed kindness to — and the abuse that made him vulnerable to her — became a global sensation through its raw honesty and refusal to simplify trauma.

title: Ripley
synopsis: Zaillian's black-and-white Highsmith adaptation follows Tom Ripley through sun-drenched Italian shadows — Andrew Scott's mesmerizing portrayal of the sociopathic charmer achieving a visual poetry that justifies yet another version of the story.

title: Black Mirror
synopsis: Brooker's anthology series holds a dark mirror to our relationship with technology — each episode a self-contained cautionary tale ranging from satirical to devastating, "San Junipero" and "White Bear" among the finest hours in television history.

title: Homeland
synopsis: Gordon and Gansa's post-9/11 thriller follows a CIA analyst convinced a returned POW has been turned — Danes's portrayal of bipolar brilliance and Damian Lewis's ambiguous loyalty creating the most gripping first season of the 2010s.

title: The Shield
synopsis: Ryan's corrupt-cop drama — Vic Mackey beating a confession from a suspect in the pilot's final scene — launched FX as a prestige network and pioneered the antihero drama that The Sopranos had inaugurated.

title: Modern Family
synopsis: Lloyd and Levitan's mockumentary about three interconnected families — traditional, blended, and same-sex — became the defining family sitcom of the 2010s, its inclusive casting both reflecting and shaping changing American attitudes.

title: Beef
synopsis: Lee's road-rage comedy follows two strangers whose parking-lot confrontation escalates into an all-consuming feud that dismantles both their lives — Yeun and Wong's performances transforming a dark comedy into a profound meditation on anger and connection.

title: Frances Ha
synopsis: Baumbach's black-and-white New York elegy follows Greta Gerwig's twenty-seven-year-old dancer Frances as her best-friendship dissolves and her adulthood refuses to start — a Truffaut-by-way-of-Brooklyn portrait of arrested becoming that announced Gerwig as a major writer-performer voice.

title: A Place in the Sun
synopsis: Stevens's Dreiser adaptation follows an ambitious young man torn between a poor factory girl and a wealthy socialite, Montgomery Clift and Elizabeth Taylor's close-ups achieving the most smoldering chemistry in 1950s cinema.

title: The Leopard
synopsis: Visconti's Palme d'Or-winning epic follows a Sicilian aristocrat watching his world dissolve during the Risorgimento — Burt Lancaster's towering performance as a man gracefully accepting obsolescence.

title: Solaris
synopsis: Tarkovsky's Soviet sci-fi masterpiece sends a psychologist to an orbital station where the ocean below materializes visitors' deepest memories — philosophical and achingly human in ways that complement Kubrick's 2001.

title: Days of Heaven
synopsis: Malick's golden-hour pastoral follows two migrant lovers scheming against a dying Texas farmer, Néstor Almendros's magic-hour cinematography creating the most visually beautiful American film of the 1970s.

title: Paris, Texas
synopsis: Wenders's American road film follows a mute wanderer emerging from the Texas desert to reconnect with his son and estranged wife — Ry Cooder's slide guitar score and Harry Dean Stanton's face telling the story words cannot.

title: Blue Velvet
synopsis: Lynch peels back small-town America to reveal a subterranean world of sadomasochism and corruption — Dennis Hopper's Frank Booth among the most terrifying villains in cinema, and Isabella Rossellini's Dorothy Vallens among the most disturbing heroines.

title: My Left Foot
synopsis: Sheridan's biography of Christy Brown — born with cerebral palsy, he painted and wrote with his left foot — features Daniel Day-Lewis's first utterly transformative performance, so committed critics wondered if it was a documentary.

title: Memento
synopsis: Nolan's breakthrough tells a murder mystery in reverse chronological order, the structure placing the audience inside the amnesiac protagonist's experience — the most ingenious structural experiment in mainstream cinema.

title: Y Tu Mamá También
synopsis: Cuarón's Mexican road trip follows two teenage boys and an older woman on a journey that begins as sexual comedy and ends as a devastating meditation on class, mortality, and the fleeting nature of youth.

title: Adaptation.
synopsis: Jonze and Kaufman's meta-comedy follows a screenwriter (played by Nicolas Cage) struggling to adapt a book about orchids — the script itself becoming the adaptation, a hall-of-mirrors that somehow generates genuine emotion.

title: The Lives of Others
synopsis: Donnersmarck's surveillance drama follows a Stasi agent who begins to sympathize with the artist couple he's monitoring — a taut thriller about the power of art to redeem even those trained to destroy it.

title: Toy Story 4
synopsis: Pixar's unlikely fourth chapter sends Woody on an existential journey that redefines his purpose beyond being a child's toy — a meditation on letting go that brings the franchise full circle.

title: Dunkirk
synopsis: Nolan's triptych-structured Dunkirk evacuation film — telling the story from land, sea, and air across different timeframes — achieves an immersive visceral experience that makes traditional war films seem literary by comparison.

title: Phantom Thread
synopsis: Anderson's haute-couture romance follows a perfectionist dressmaker whose ordered life is disrupted by his new muse — Daniel Day-Lewis's final performance, a study in controlled obsession that ranks among his greatest.

title: Black Panther
synopsis: Coogler's Afrofuturist superhero film brought Wakanda to the global mainstream — a cultural phenomenon whose Afrocentric world-building, Killmonger's compelling villainy, and Kendrick Lamar's soundtrack made it the first superhero film nominated for Best Picture.

title: Soul
synopsis: Pixar's most philosophically ambitious film follows a jazz musician into the afterlife's bureaucracy — its meditation on what makes life worth living transcending the children's-film format entirely.

title: Before Sunset
synopsis: Linklater's real-time sequel reunites Ethan Hawke's Jesse and Julie Delpy's Céline nine years after their Vienna night — an eighty-minute walk through Paris that becomes one of the most precisely written romantic two-handers in modern cinema, ending on the year's most quoted last line.

title: Licorice Pizza
synopsis: Anderson's 1970s San Fernando Valley romance follows a teenager pursuing a twenty-something woman through a series of entrepreneurial misadventures — sun-drenched nostalgia suffused with genuine tenderness.

title: Ikiru
synopsis: Kurosawa's humanist masterwork follows Watanabe — a stamp-pushing Tokyo bureaucrat diagnosed with terminal stomach cancer — through a final attempt at meaning that pivots on building a children's playground in a flooded slum, the famous snow-covered swing scene one of the most quoted shots in all of cinema.

title: Oz
synopsis: Fontana's brutal prison drama was HBO's first original hour-long series, its unflinching depiction of life inside a maximum-security facility laying the creative groundwork for The Sopranos and everything that followed.

title: South Park
synopsis: Trey Parker and Matt Stone's South Park has sustained a singular formal audacity for nearly three decades — its six-day production cycle allowing the show to satirize the week's cultural eruptions with a speed and viciousness no other comedy can match. The four Colorado fourth-graders — Stan, Kyle, Cartman, and Kenny — are among the most recognizable characters in the history of American animation, while the show's willingness to skewer every ideology equally, and its escalating formal invention from 'Imaginationland' to the serialized Trump-era seasons, make it the most consistently provocative satire on television.

title: Chappelle's Show
synopsis: Dave Chappelle and Neal Brennan's sketch comedy series achieved the rarest of things — a show whose cultural penetration was so total that its creator walked away from a $50 million contract rather than compromise it. The sketches — the blind Black white supremacist, the pixie drug dealer, Charlie Murphy's Prince story, the player-hater's ball — entered the American vernacular permanently. Chappelle's willingness to confront race, class, and celebrity with a diagnostic honesty that made white and Black audiences laugh at different things simultaneously remains the most sophisticated racial comedy in television history.

title: Killing Eve
synopsis: Waller-Bridge's adaptation follows an MI5 agent and a psychopathic assassin in a cat-and-mouse obsession that blurs the line between hunter and hunted — Comer's Villanelle becoming the most iconic TV villain of the decade.

title: BoJack Horseman
synopsis: Raphael Bob-Waksberg's Netflix animated series deployed its half-man, half-horse washed-up TV star to mount the most sustained and rigorous exploration of depression, addiction, self-destruction, and the impossibility of forgiveness in the history of American animation. Lisa Hanawalt's art direction created a pastel-colored Los Angeles in which the absurdity of anthropomorphic animals performing celebrity culture only deepened the show's emotional accuracy — its sixth and final season achieving a devastating clarity that most dramas never reach.

title: Community
synopsis: Dan Harmon's Community is the most formally adventurous network sitcom of the 21st century — a show that treated its Greendale Community College setting as a platform for extended genre experiments (a Western, a documentary, a zombie movie, an 8-bit video game, a stop-motion Christmas special) while maintaining genuine emotional investment in its characters. Its influence on the generation of comedy writers who have defined the following decade — including Donald Glover, whose Atlanta carries Community's DNA directly — makes it among the most consequential sitcoms never to win an Emmy.

title: Yellowjackets
synopsis: Lyle and Nickerson's dual-timeline thriller follows a girls' soccer team stranded in the wilderness — the present revealing that whatever happened out there was worse than anyone imagined.

title: House of Cards
synopsis: Netflix's first prestige drama — Kevin Spacey's Machiavellian congressman climbing to the presidency through manipulation and murder — proved streaming could produce television as ambitious as HBO's best.

title: Orange Is the New Black
synopsis: Kohan's women's-prison dramedy achieved something few shows manage — genuine diversity and intersectionality that felt organic rather than programmatic, its ensemble becoming Netflix's first cultural touchstone.

title: Nosferatu
synopsis: Murnau's unauthorized Dracula adaptation created cinema's most unsettling vampire — Max Schreck's Count Orlok, rat-faced and shadow-clawed, so nightmarish that a court ordered all prints destroyed, yet the film survived to become horror's foundational text.

title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari
synopsis: Wiene's painted-shadow nightmare — a mad doctor who controls a sleepwalker to commit murders — invented German Expressionism in cinema and established horror as a legitimate genre with its radical visual distortions.

title: The Gold Rush
synopsis: Chaplin's Klondike comedy — the bread-roll dance, the shoe-eating, the teetering cabin — was the film he wanted to be remembered by, its blend of slapstick and pathos establishing the template for all comedy that aspires to art.

title: Intolerance
synopsis: Griffith's staggering four-story epic intercuts narratives across 2,500 years of history — ancient Babylon, the life of Christ, 16th-century France, and modern America — creating cross-cutting montage techniques that became the grammar of cinema.

title: Aguirre, the Wrath of God
synopsis: Herzog's hallucinatory masterpiece follows a mad conquistador leading his men deeper into the Amazon in pursuit of El Dorado — Klaus Kinski's deranged performance and the actual-jungle production creating cinema's most vivid portrait of obsession.

title: The Thin Red Line
synopsis: Malick's return after twenty years transformed a WWII Guadalcanal battle into a philosophical meditation on nature, violence, and transcendence — its all-star cast subsumed into landscapes and voiceover that achieve something closer to poetry than narrative.

title: Zodiac
synopsis: Fincher's meticulous procedural follows the decades-long hunt for the Zodiac killer — the investigation itself becoming a portrait of American obsession, its lack of resolution the point rather than the problem.

title: The Tree of Life
synopsis: Malick's cosmic meditation on grace, nature, and a 1950s Texas childhood expands outward to encompass the birth of the universe and the death of the sun — the most formally ambitious American film since 2001.

title: Blade Runner 2049
synopsis: Villeneuve's visually staggering sequel expands the Blade Runner universe with a new replicant detective searching for a miracle — Roger Deakins's cinematography earning the long-overdue Oscar and establishing the film as a rare sequel that deepens its predecessor.

title: A Hard Day's Night
synopsis: Lester's pseudo-documentary records thirty-six hours in the Beatles' lives at the peak of Beatlemania — train escapes, press conferences, Wilfrid Brambell's "very clean" grandfather, and a closing TV concert — using a kind of jump-cut energy and direct-to-camera cheek that pre-invented MTV by two decades.

title: Ford v Ferrari
synopsis: Mangold's Le Mans epic follows Carroll Shelby and Ken Miles building a car to beat Ferrari at the 1966 24 Hours — Bale and Damon's chemistry and the thunderous race sequences making it the finest motorsport film ever.

title: The Royal Tenenbaums
synopsis: Anderson's symmetrical family epic gathers the prodigal Tenenbaum children — failed tennis star, neurotic financier, melancholy adopted playwright — back to a New York brownstone under Gene Hackman's manipulative father returning with a feigned terminal illness, a deadpan-comic group portrait that became the visual grammar of indie cinema for a decade.

title: Almost Famous
synopsis: Crowe's lightly fictionalized memoir sends Patrick Fugit's teenage rock journalist on the road with Stillwater, Billy Crudup's magnetic guitarist and Kate Hudson's Penny Lane orbiting the page — a film about the moment when fandom turns into both criticism and grief, and one of the warmest portraits of 1970s rock-and-roll on film.

title: Easy Rider
synopsis: Hopper and Fonda's motorcycle odyssey from Mexico to Mardi Gras through a hostile American South — Jack Nicholson's breakthrough as a country lawyer, the soundtrack of Steppenwolf and The Byrds, the unflinching ending — detonated the studio system and ushered in the New Hollywood era.

title: Harakiri
synopsis: Kobayashi's anti-bushido masterpiece begins with a ronin (Tatsuya Nakadai) arriving at a feudal lord's estate to request honorable seppuku and unfolds, through flashback, into a methodical demolition of samurai-code hypocrisy — every measured frame a cold rebuke of the institution it ostensibly dramatizes.

title: Ugetsu
synopsis: Mizoguchi's ghost-haunted Sengoku-era parable follows a potter who abandons his wife for the promise of fortune and is seduced by an aristocratic spirit, while his brother-in-law's vanity-driven pursuit of samurai status destroys their two households — a film whose mist-drenched cinematography and crane-shot grace are studied as the apex of long-take filmmaking.

title: Andrei Rublev
synopsis: Tarkovsky's eight-part epic on the 15th-century icon painter Andrei Rublev journeys through a medieval Russia of pagan rites, Tatar raids, bell-casting villages, and theological doubt — a film whose long-take spirituality, monumental compositions, and final color-burst into Rublev's actual icons is studied as the cathedral of the long-take tradition.

title: Stalker
synopsis: Tarkovsky's post-apocalyptic parable follows an illegal guide — the Stalker — leading a Writer and a Professor through the forbidden Zone toward a Room said to grant innermost desires, the long-take, rain-drenched journey collapsing science fiction into theology and one of cinema's most studied meditations on faith.

title: Peaky Blinders
synopsis: Knight's Birmingham crime saga follows the Shelby family from post-WWI razor gangs to interwar power brokers — Cillian Murphy's Thomas Shelby becoming one of TV's most iconic antiheroes.

title: Shogun (1980)
synopsis: London's adaptation of Clavell's novel brought feudal Japan to mainstream American television with unprecedented production values — Richard Chamberlain and Toshiro Mifune headlining a cultural event that captured the nation.

title: Brideshead Revisited
synopsis: Sturridge's faithful Waugh adaptation follows Charles Ryder's entanglement with the aristocratic Marchmain family across two decades — Jeremy Irons's breakout performance and the Oxford and Venice locations creating British television's most ravishing production.

title: The Night Manager
synopsis: Bier's le Carré adaptation follows a hotel night manager recruited by intelligence to infiltrate an arms dealer's inner circle — Hugh Laurie's silky villain and Hiddleston's physical commitment creating the best le Carré screen adaptation since Smiley.

title: Mindhunter
synopsis: Fincher's procedural follows FBI agents pioneering criminal profiling in the late 1970s — its interviews with real serial killers achieving a level of sustained, quiet dread that makes it the most cerebral crime series ever produced.

title: The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel
synopsis: Sherman-Palladino's 1950s-set comedy follows a Jewish housewife who discovers she's a brilliant stand-up comedian — Rachel Brosnahan's effervescent performance and the show's dazzling period production making it Amazon's signature series.

title: Normal People
synopsis: Sally Rooney's will-they/won't-they follows Connell and Marianne from Sligo secondary school through Trinity College — Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones's intimate performances creating the most emotionally naked romance on television.

title: Mare of Easttown
synopsis: Zobel's Pennsylvania small-town mystery follows a detective investigating a murder while grappling with personal loss — Winslet's deglammed, emotionally raw performance making it the surprise cultural event of spring 2021.

title: Hacks
dir: Lucia Aniello, Paul W. Downs, Jen Statsky (creators)
synopsis: Aniello, Downs, and Statsky's comedy pairs a legendary Las Vegas comedian with a young comedy writer, their generational clash generating both hilarious friction and genuine emotional depth — Jean Smart's Deborah Vance a career-defining triumph.

title: Pachinko
synopsis: Hugh's adaptation of Min Jin Lee's novel spans four generations of a Korean family from Japanese-occupied Korea to 1980s Japan and modern New York — Lee Min-ho and Youn Yuh-jung anchoring a sweeping immigrant epic.

title: Andor
synopsis: Gilroy's Star Wars prequel follows Cassian Andor's radicalization from petty thief to rebel spy — a le Carré-style espionage drama set in a galaxy far away that became the best-reviewed Star Wars content in a generation.

title: Reservation Dogs
synopsis: Harjo and Waititi created the first series with an entirely Indigenous writers' room and directing slate — four Native teens in rural Oklahoma navigating adolescence and grief with humor, myth, and a specificity that feels universal.

title: Shrinking
dir: Bill Lawrence, Brett Goldstein, Jason Segel (creators)
synopsis: Lawrence, Goldstein, and Segel's therapy comedy follows a grieving psychologist who starts telling his patients what he really thinks — Harrison Ford's scene-stealing TV debut as a grumpy neighbor therapist proving legends can still surprise.

title: Birdman
synopsis: Iñárritu's backstage comedy follows a washed-up superhero actor mounting a Broadway play to reclaim artistic legitimacy — the film's apparent single-take construction creating a virtuosic high-wire act.

title: Children of Men
synopsis: Cuarón's near-future dystopia: in 2027 humanity faces extinction from mass infertility, and a cynical bureaucrat (Clive Owen) is conscripted to escort the world's only pregnant woman to safety across a fascist Britain — staged in long, unbroken takes that placed the camera inside the chaos.

title: Little Women
synopsis: Gerwig's non-linear adaptation liberates Alcott's novel from period-piece conventions by intercutting the March sisters' youth and adulthood — Saoirse Ronan's Jo March burning with creative ambition that feels urgently modern.

title: A Separation
synopsis: Farhadi's morally seismic Tehran drama follows a middle-class couple's separation as it spirals — through a misdiagnosed pregnancy, a class collision with the religious caregiver hired for the husband's Alzheimer's-stricken father, and a courtroom where every account is partial — into one of the most precisely observed ethical thrillers in modern cinema.

title: A Quiet Place
synopsis: Krasinski's high-concept horror follows a family surviving in silence to avoid sound-hunting creatures — Emily Blunt's bathtub labor scene achieving the most sustained tension in modern horror.

title: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
synopsis: The Coens' Depression-era Mississippi Odyssey sends George Clooney's vain Ulysses Everett McGill and two fellow chain-gang escapees rambling through bluegrass-and-Klan-rally Americana — the first widely seen feature shot mostly digitally then color-graded to sepia, scored by a folk-revival songbook that became a Grammy-winning cultural phenomenon.

title: Mission: Impossible – Fallout
synopsis: McQuarrie's sixth Mission: Impossible delivers the most physically demanding action film of the decade — Cruise actually HALO jumping, breaking his ankle on camera, and flying a helicopter — proving that practical stunt filmmaking at its peak remains cinema's most thrilling spectacle.

title: Tar
synopsis: Field's drama follows a legendary conductor facing a reckoning — Blanchett's Lydia Tár the most forensic character study of power since Citizen Kane.

title: Manhattan
synopsis: Allen's love letter to New York follows a comedy writer navigating romantic entanglements against Gordon Willis's stunning black-and-white Manhattan skyline — Gershwin's "Rhapsody in Blue" making the city itself the film's greatest character.

title: The Birds
synopsis: Hitchcock's apocalyptic horror follows an unexplained bird attack on a California coastal town — the absence of a musical score and the pioneering electronic sound design creating cinema's most unsettling ecological nightmare.

title: Casino
synopsis: Scorsese's Las Vegas epic follows the rise and fall of a mob-backed casino operator — De Niro, Pesci, and Stone combusting in a three-hour portrait of American excess and institutional corruption.

title: Rio Bravo
synopsis: Hawks's leisurely masterpiece follows a sheriff, a drunk, an old man, and a young gunslinger defending a jail against outlaws — the film that invented the "hang-out movie" where character interaction matters more than plot.

title: Godzilla Minus One
synopsis: Yamazaki's Godzilla channels postwar Japanese trauma into the most emotionally devastating kaiju film ever made — defeating Hollywood blockbusters to win the VFX Oscar on a fraction of their budget.

title: The Boy and the Heron
synopsis: Miyazaki's purported final film follows a boy grieving his mother into a fantastical tower inhabited by a mysterious heron — the master animator's most personal and abstractly beautiful work.

title: Chungking Express
synopsis: Wong's two-story diptych of lovelorn Hong Kong police officers — Takeshi Kaneshiro's cop pining over canned pineapple expirations, Tony Leung's cop oblivious to Faye Wong's snack-shop crush — moves on hand-held momentum and California Dreamin' through a Mid-Levels of nighttime escalators and 24-hour stalls, the film that introduced Wong to the West.

title: Safe
synopsis: Haynes's clinical San Fernando Valley horror film follows Julianne Moore's suburban housewife Carol White as she develops a mysterious environmental illness that no one — doctors, family, the desert wellness commune she eventually joins — can definitively name, treat, or believe in.

title: Hannah and Her Sisters
synopsis: Allen's warmest comedy weaves three sisters' romantic and existential crises across two Thanksgivings — Michael Caine and Dianne Wiest both winning Oscars in an ensemble piece that represents Allen's most generous vision of human connection.

title: Rope
synopsis: Hitchcock's technical experiment confines the audience to a single Manhattan apartment where two young men host a dinner party with the body of their victim hidden in a chest — the film's apparent single-take construction a high-wire act of sustained suspense.

title: Inside Llewyn Davis
synopsis: The Coens' melancholy 1961 Greenwich Village odyssey follows a struggling folk singer (Oscar Isaac) through one circular week of couches, missed buses, a ginger cat, and a marble-mouthed John Goodman — a portrait of pre-fame folk-revival drift soundtracked by some of the most fully realized music in any modern American film.

title: Once Upon a Time in the West
synopsis: Leone's monumental Spaghetti Western opens with three gunmen waiting on a train platform and unspools over nearly three hours into a railroad-versus-frontier mythography — Charles Bronson's harmonica-playing avenger, Henry Fonda cast against type as a child-killer, Claudia Cardinale's widow holding the land everyone wants — scored by Ennio Morricone in arguably the greatest film score ever composed.

title: Yi Yi
synopsis: Yang's nearly three-hour Taipei family chronicle moves between an engineer (NJ) at midlife, his comatose mother-in-law, his teenage daughter, and his eight-year-old son Yang-Yang — whose photographs of the backs of people's heads become the film's emblem of seeing what others cannot.

title: Oldboy
synopsis: Park's mid-trilogy revenge masterpiece imprisons Choi Min-sik's Oh Dae-su for fifteen years in a hotel-room cell without explanation, then releases him with five days to find his captor — a hammer-corridor brawl, a live-octopus meal, and a final-act revelation that broke the South Korean wave wide open internationally.
